notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: The first initiative I took during my journey to search for a college was choosing my major. Fortunately, this decision has been clear to me for several years now, as I have always wanted to study nursing. I chose to pursue a degree in nursing for several reasons, both moral and logical. Initially, I have always had an extreme sense of empathy for others. Many of my close friends and family often say that I have too much sympathy for people, but I believe that this trait is very necessary in a nurse. I absolutely love to serve others; the ability to have a positive impact on others makes me very excited. Additionally, I have always excelled at math and science, and I take a particular interest in biology and human anatomy. After taking such a liking to these subjects throughout high school, I knew that a career in the science field would be suitable for me. By considering both my willingness to help others and my success in the sciences, I decided to pursue a degree in nursing. Nursing is also an extremely valuable degree right now because it is so versatile; there is an abundance of career choices you are able to pursue with a Bachelor’s of Science in Nursing. Eventually, I hope to attend graduate school and become either a Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist or a Nurse Practitioner, but I will see where nursing school takes me before making a decision as to which career path I will take. I am extremely passionate about healthcare because of the emotional benefits that I will gain from helping others.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: MED has so many benefits to offer to pre-nursing students that will help me succeed in the program. Initially, there are multiple brothers in MED who are currently enrolled in the nursing program at the University of Tampa. These students have already gone through the entire process of completing all the prerequisites, applying, and being accepted. By joining MED, I will have the opportunity to form close connections with these students and ask them for advice. Additionally, joining MED will give me the chance to form new friendships with like-minded people who are driven to succeed. Being a healthcare major is not easy, and it requires long hours of studying and work. By becoming a member of MED, I am hoping to feel supported and gain more motivation from people who are in similar situations as me. It is very important to me to have friends with similar work ethics and academic drives, as we can encourage each other to become better. Additionally, I am hoping to gain valuable service experience from MED that I will use to help me succeed in my major and career. Service is something that I value very much, and getting to volunteer in medical settings will help me gain more of the experience that will be needed to work in a hospital. Overall, I hope to gain valuable connections, friendships, and service experience from MED.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: Along with my devout passion for nursing, I also possess many skills and traits that would enhance mine and others’ experiences in MED. Initially, I pride myself most in my strong work ethic. My friends and family often compliment my drive and ability to overcome any task that I am faced with. Not only do I complete required tasks to my best effort, I am also constantly giving myself more to accomplish. As the oldest child, I have always been an extremely high achiever; everything has to be done, and it has to be done perfectly. Alongside my strong work ethic, I also have adequate time management skills. No matter how much I have to accomplish in a day, I ensure that I have time to complete every task. As a member of MED, I will use these skills to assist in planning events and fundraisers, as well as ensuring my presence at each and every outing. Additionally, I have very strong leadership skills that I intend to use when pursuing a leadership position in this organization. I was the captain of the field hockey and lacrosse team during high school, as well as the president of Key Club, so I am very good at organizing events for causes that I am passionate about. As someone with a very strong work ethic, time management, and leadership skills, I will ensure to put my utmost effort into the events that MED has to offer.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
Various jobs, volunteer experiences, and other extracurriculars that I have participated in throughout high school have prepared me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare. Initially, I have been a member of the high school field hockey and lacrosse team since seventh grade, and I have also participated in a variety of youth sports prior to that. As a member of a sports team, I learned how to communicate and work with others very well. During games, my teammates and I would occasionally disagree on what decisions to make, but we would always end up making the choice that supported the entire team rather than an individual person. By playing sports, I learned to put others before myself and collaborate in order to achieve success. This skill is vital in a career in healthcare because I will be working in a hospital with an abundance of other nurses, doctors, and other healthcare staff that I will need to communicate with in order to ensure the safety of my patients. With such a large number of people working on a floor, we are also bound to get into disagreements sometimes, but playing sports taught me how to make the right decision by putting others over myself and looking at the bigger picture. Playing sports mainly prepared me for the collaborative aspect of a career in healthcare. 
	Additionally, my job as a food runner prepared me for the fast-paced nature of a career in healthcare. I often worked long, busy hours with no breaks where I was constantly bringing food from one table to the next. Because of this, I have valuable critical thinking skills and I work well under pressure. Instead of breaking down, I flourish when put into a stressful situation, which is an essential trait in a career in healthcare, especially when patients’ lives are at stake. This job could often be physically and mentally demanding; however, I am extremely grateful that the fast-paced nature of this work environment prepared me for this aspect of the healthcare industry. Throughout high school, I participated in a variety of jobs, volunteer experiences, and extracurriculars that have prepared me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose my major because ever since I was a little kid, I always knew I wanted to go into a profession where I could help others. At different points in my life, I wanted to be a teacher, a psychologist, and eventually a doctor. Whenever a friend or family member was sick or hurt, I found myself wanting to be there for them, whether that meant helping with an injury, checking on them, or simply making sure they felt cared for. I have always found a lot of meaning in being someone others can rely on. When I first applied to college, I was unsure of exactly what I wanted to do, so I explored psychology. Although I enjoyed learning about people and understanding why we think and behave the way we do, I still felt like something was missing. I kept coming back to my interest in medicine and the direct impact healthcare professionals can have on someone's life. That feeling led me toward my current major and my interest in pursuing a career as a Physician Assistant. What excites me most about healthcare is the combination of science and human connection. I want a career where I can continue learning while also building relationships with the people I am helping. I know I still have a lot to learn about the different paths within healthcare, and I am excited to explore them. Ultimately, I want to enter a field where I can make people feel heard, supported, and cared for during some of the most hardest moments of their lives.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I am interested in joining MED because I really want to be surrounded by more like-minded individuals who are also career focused and passionate about healthcare. Our school lacks the proper community and support for pre-health students so I was extremely excited when this fraternity was created. I am hoping to gain a better understanding of the different opportunities and paths within healthcare through MED. While I am currently very interested in becoming a Physician Assistant, I know that there is still so much about the healthcare field that I have yet to experience and learn about. I hope to make meaningful relationships and connections through this fraternity. I think having people around me who share similar goals and interests will help motivate me throughout college and as I work toward my career. I would love the opportunity to learn from other members about their experiences, get advice about preparing for a career in healthcare, and eventually being able to provide that same support to newer members. I also want to take advantage of the volunteer opportunities that MED provides so I can gain more hands-on exposure to some different areas of the medical field while helping the community. I am excited to learn from guest speakers and hear about their experiences and career paths, and hopefully be able to shadow a few of them. I am excited about possibly utilizing the resources and connections MED can provide by meeting healthcare professionals and other students who can help me learn more about the field. I think these experiences and connections would help me explore my interests and better understand what I want my future in healthcare to look like.

I am very excited to get involved, help wherever I can, and build relationships with other members who have similar goals. I am still figuring out exactly where I want to go in healthcare, but I know that this is something I am truly passionate about and want to pursue. I would love the opportunity to show my motivation and willingness to learn and grow. I am also very goal-oriented and ambitious, so when I set my mind to something I don’t like giving up when it gets difficult. I hold myself to high standards and am always looking for ways to improve, whether that is in school, my future career, or as a person. I think one of my strengths is that I genuinely enjoy getting to know people and forming connections so I really want to be surrounded by people who motivate me to be better, and I want to be that person for others as well. I think my work ethic, determination, and ability to connect with people would allow me to bring a lot to MED while also continuing to grow within the fraternity.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences working and volunteering have helped me develop skills that I know will be important in a career in healthcare. One of the most meaningful experiences I have had was volunteering at Cleveland Clinic. I helped stock inpatient rooms and assisted nurses with different tasks, but one of my favorite parts was being able to interact with patients. Even though some of my responsibilities were small, being around patients and seeing how nurses cared for them gave me a better understanding of how important compassion, communication, and patience are in healthcare. It also made me more excited about wanting to work in a field where I can directly help people. Working at Hollister and HomeGoods has also taught me a lot about interacting with people. I have had to learn how to communicate with all different types of customers, work with my coworkers, and stay calm when things get busy. Sometimes it’s as simple as listening to someone and figuring out what they need but I have learned that those small interactions can make a difference in someone's experience. I think that will carry over into healthcare because being able to talk to patients and make them feel comfortable is something I really value. I also volunteered at a church a few days before Thanksgiving to help give out canned and boxed meals to families in the community. I liked being able to see the people we were helping and knowing that the time we spent preparing and handing out meals was going directly toward helping families during the holidays. It made volunteering feel less like something I was doing for the hours and more like something I genuinely enjoyed doing. Overall, these experiences have given me different opportunities to work with and care for people. My experience at the Cleveland Clinic especially helped me realize that I want a career where I can have that kind of interaction with patients every day. I know healthcare will come with challenges, but these experiences have made me excited to pursue medicine and help others every day.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: My interest in healthcare began at a young age through an experience that had a lasting impact on me. My best friend growing up was diagnosed with DIPG, a rare and aggressive brain tumor. Watching her go through treatment and eventually losing her made me look at medicine in a completely different way. I became curious about how something within the brain could change a person’s life so quickly, why some diseases are so difficult to treat, and how much there is still to learn about the human body. My own experiences also played a major role in why I chose psychology. Throughout middle and high school, I struggled with my mental health, and later being diagnosed with ADHD and anxiety helped me better understand many of those experiences. It made me increasingly interested in how the brain affects attention, emotions, behavior, and everyday functioning. That curiosity is what led me to pursue a B.S. in Psychology. I am especially drawn to the biological side of psychology, particularly biopsychology, neuroscience, and neurology, because I enjoy understanding the connection between the brain, behavior, and physical health. My long-term goal is to attend medical school and pursue a career in medicine. Choosing the B.S. track gives me the opportunity to build a stronger scientific foundation while continuing to study the areas of psychology that interest me most. Throughout high school, mentors and role models in my life also encouraged me to consider medicine because they saw how naturally I connected with people and how genuinely interested I was in science and healthcare. What makes me passionate about healthcare is the combination of science and human connection. I want a career where I can continue learning, understand people on a deeper level, and make a meaningful difference in their lives.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: What I hope to gain most from MED is a community of people who understand the path I am working toward. I do not have many people in my life who have gone through the medical school or healthcare route, and most of my close friends are pursuing business-related majors. While I value those friendships, I would really like to be surrounded by students who share similar academic goals, interests, and challenges. I think being part of MED would give me the opportunity to learn from people who are further along in the pre-health process and gain guidance that I have not always had access to. I would especially value mentorship from students who can offer advice about classes, clinical experience, research, medical school preparation, and the different opportunities available within healthcare. As an international student, I also hope MED can help me become more connected to the Tampa community and learn about meaningful ways to get involved off campus. Finding volunteer, clinical, or service opportunities can sometimes feel more difficult when you are still learning the area and building a network, so having guidance from members who are familiar with local opportunities would be extremely valuable to me. Most importantly, I hope to build genuine relationships with like-minded people who can support and motivate one another. I want MED to be more than just another organization I join. I hope it becomes a community where I can grow, contribute, learn from others, and feel more confident as I continue working toward a future in medicine.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: One of the strongest qualities I would bring to MED is empathy. I genuinely enjoy connecting with people and making others feel supported, comfortable, and included. I believe this is especially valuable in a healthcare-focused organization, where understanding and working well with others is just as important as academic success. Leadership is another major strength I would contribute. Throughout high school, athletics played a large role in shaping the person I am today. I served as a captain for my club volleyball team as well as my high school basketball, volleyball, and golf teams. Being trusted with leadership roles across different teams taught me that leadership is not simply about being the loudest person or telling others what to do. I learned how to communicate with different personalities, motivate teammates when morale was low, stay composed under pressure, and recognize when someone needed encouragement rather than criticism. Being part of competitive teams also taught me accountability and reliability. Other people depended on me to show up prepared, put in effort, and contribute even when things were difficult. Those experiences helped me become comfortable working toward a common goal while still recognizing the individual strengths of the people around me. I would bring that same mindset to MED. I am motivated, outgoing, dependable, and always willing to learn from others. I would want to be someone who actively participates rather than simply having my name on the membership list. Most importantly, I would contribute to creating a supportive environment where members feel encouraged to challenge themselves, celebrate one another’s accomplishments, and work together toward their goals in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: One of the experiences that has prepared me most for a career in healthcare has been volunteering at Sunnybrook’s St. John’s Rehabilitation Centre in Toronto. Through this role, I have had the opportunity to work around patients recovering from life-changing conditions and injuries, including amputations, cardiac conditions, major trauma, and burns. Being in a rehabilitation environment has allowed me to see patient care from a much more personal perspective. Recovery is often a long and difficult process, and each patient comes in with different physical abilities, emotions, goals, and challenges. My responsibilities include assisting patients, staff, and visitors, transporting patients throughout the centre, helping maintain and disinfect rehabilitation equipment, and supporting a safe and professional environment. These responsibilities have taught me that patient care is not limited to major medical procedures. It also means helping patients feel comfortable, respected, safe, and supported throughout their recovery. Working with patients who are going through such difficult periods in their lives has especially taught me patience. I have learned that recovery does not happen at the same pace for everyone, and that frustration, fear, pain, and uncertainty can affect how a patient communicates or responds. This experience has taught me to slow down, listen carefully, and approach each person with understanding rather than assumptions. It has also shown me how collaborative healthcare is. I have been able to observe how physicians, nurses, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, and other healthcare professionals work together to support each patient’s recovery and independence. Most importantly, volunteering at Sunnybrook has reinforced how strongly I want to work in healthcare. Seeing both the physical and emotional sides of recovery has made the field feel even more meaningful to me. It has shown me that healthcare requires compassion, professionalism, patience, communication, and a genuine commitment to patient care, and those are qualities I hope to continue developing throughout my path toward medicine. Service has also been an important part of my life outside of Sunnybrook. In high school, I received the Lieutenant Governor’s Community Volunteer Award in recognition of my volunteer service. Receiving this award was meaningful to me because it represented the time I had dedicated to helping others and reinforced how much I value being involved in my community.

So, I think all of these experiences have helped shape me into the person I am today and made me realize not exactly what I want to do but put me on the right track.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: Growing up, I had always been an all-sports and general athletics person, trying many different ones and sticking with soccer and basketball for 13 years. My growing love for being recognized for my athletic performances is what continued to drive me to stay involved and improve my abilities. When I got into high school, sports became the most serious they had ever been. By following advice and information through coaches and athletic trainers when I had been injured, I realized the amount of knowledge you have of how your body works can have a huge helpful impact on athletes and general exercisers. Knowing facts about nutrition and anatomy can allow one to improve their methods, leading them to better successes and less chance of injury. My interest in the healthcare field stemmed from being an athlete myself, but as I matured, it grew into a yearn and desire of helping younger athletes, like I was, get back to doing what they love. Learning the true inner workings of our bodies can give you so much more help when it comes to understanding injuries, prevention, and recovery. Senior year is when I discovered the PA field and it immediately drew me in. Working as a healthcare professional focused on sports medicine to make a meaningful difference in adolescents’ and young adults’ lives seemed like something that would never feel like work for me. Wanting to help people figure out what the problem was and ways to fix it so they can do what they love again came from me being in those exact same shoes many times. It combined something I’ve always been passionate about and a newfound interest that developed through my own experience. Being a sports-medicine focused PA allows me to help kids like myself.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: As a sophomore college student pursuing a career in healthcare, I can’t see why someone wouldn’t want to be involved in an organization like MED with all that it has to offer. One of the most valuable aspects of joining this fraternity, and what almost every current member mentioned as their favorite part, is the community you can gain. A group of like-minded students with the same goals, drives, and even struggles can all help and support each other through their journeys. A traditional sorority was never really my type of vibe, but with MED, you have the opportunity to connect or be connected with peers, upperclassmen, alumni, and healthcare professionals who can offer guidance, resources, mentorship, accessibility, and more. All of which can benefit my career journey. You can also learn from other’s experiences and certain do’s and don’ts to help yourself in the future and better prepare for what’s to come. I am also so interested in the hands-on experience opportunities that are often set up for the members of the frat. I have the ability to give back to my new community and promote health and wellness while improving my own skills and knowledge for my career. I also hope to develop interpersonal and communication skills with others on a professional healthcare-based level. All healthcare professionals work closely with patients and employees that are a part of their teams, which makes these skills essential for me to practice and improve.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: As a second year college student who has grown up prioritizing health, wellness, and exercise, there are many attributes I’ve acquired that I could bring to positively contribute to MED if I became a brother. Through my lifelong involvement in sports, I have developed strong leadership, teamwork, time management, organization, and communication skills are essential in both student and professional healthcare organizations. Building a foundation of qualities like these have prepared me to be a part of a group like MED, and potentially earn and thrive in a leadership position. MED and the healthcare field in general requires understanding the importance of discipline, dedication, and perseverance. All my life I’ve had to balance academics, athletics, clubs, sociability, and personal responsibilities, and recently part time jobs. I could contribute by helping organize fraternity events, service and volunteer projects, attend speaker events, encourage my peers, resolve challenges, and support all other members. I am also eager to participate in health-related volunteer work, listen to professional speakers, and further my knowledge for my future career. Aside from developed skills, I am a very compassionate, caring, and supportive person. I have a really big heart, and I know I can be someone members trust coming to for support and advice, as well as being the type of person you want as a volunteer when helping the community. As a member of this fraternity, I would have the opportunity to showcase that I am someone who is passionate about this field and about the overall mission of healthcare. I would be an asset to MED as another individual who is exactly the type of person you want representing what this fraternity is about, and because of these specific attributes and skills I can bring and demonstrate to help the fraternity become even just 1% better.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: Through all of my involvement in the many jobs, volunteer work, and other affiliations, I have learned and practiced a numerous amount of skills that can directly relate to what is needed from an individual looking to go into healthcare. I’ve had many customer service positions due to my part time jobs at the UT fitness center, Joe & The Juice, and Tropical Smoothie. Over the years of working these positions, I have developed professionalism, patience, communication, problem solving, and other interpersonal skills by assisting thousands of customers, resolving concerns, and creating positive experiences to gain customer loyalty. These roles have also taught me how to function and manage in high stress and fast paced environments, like what a healthcare environment would be. As a Bike UT attendant, I have to prioritize rider safety and pay close attention to detail when inspecting the bikes, which is a quality essential to healthcare work. The volunteer experiences I’ve completed have helped to develop my leadership skills and further developed my compassion and commitment to helping others. For example, coaching and refereeing youth sports taught me how to interact with little kids, educating and supporting them while teaching the importance of teamwork. And volunteering with homeless outreach organizations opened my eyes to see the different vulnerable populations of a community, giving me first-hand experience of serving with empathy and respect. Additionally, being a part of multiple organizations such as high school sports and clubs, college club soccer, and UT healthcare focused clubs gave me a real taste of what my life will be centered around if I make it into the career I desire: Sports Medicine. I’ve been exposed to all things sports and fitness through my passion and participation, and the clubs I chose to be in have presented different healthcare paths, experiences, and emphasized what it means and what it takes to help others. Everything I’ve ever been a part of has only improved me as a human being, preparing me for an incredibly important healthcare career and reinforcing my desire to make it there and help others improve their health.

candidates.name: Amelia Grace Schoneweis

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose my major because it is the best foundation for the graduate programs I want to apply to. Aside from that, I have always loved science and knew my major in college would be centered around it. I came into UT as a biology major and then switched to Allied Health because it offers more of the prerequisite courses I need for graduate programs like PA or AA schools. I am passionate about healthcare because I have always showed my love through caring for those around me. I love helping my friends and family with anything they need. I always knew I wanted to continue my love for helping others through my future career. Healthcare is the avenue that I can do this in. I have seen it become a large part of many of my family members lives in terms of receiving the healthcare. Although the circumstances are not always what they wanted, the interactions with the people who work in healthcare have made their experiences memorable and amazing. I hope to one day be able to make my patients' experiences just as amazing.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I view MED as an opportunity to continue to grow as a person, specifically growing my involvement in healthcare whether that be through the amazing weekly volunteer opportunities or the research opportunities that are offered to members in MED. I also see MED as a great community and got to hear first hand at the introduction meeting, by all the members who talked about how much they love the MED community. At UT I only have one friend who is a science major. The rest of my friends are all business majors. I would really love to have more friends who have like minded goals, centered around a future career in healthcare. I also really like all the fun events MED does. Things like pickleball allow you to hangout with your friends, while also taking your mind off all the stress from school, for a little while. The study sessions really stuck out to me because in MED everyone is taking somewhat of the same courses, so everyone can help each other and it is so good to talk things out with people who have already gone through it. MED seems like it makes the pre-health journey a little less daunting and along the way allows you to have a wonderful like-minded community and that is why I would love to be a part of it.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I have always been someone who is an empath. Although sometimes it is looked down upon I have always seen it as a good thing. The pre-health track can be extremely stressful and tiring. As an empath I can put myself in their shoes even if we are on different pre tracks, in the end we are both pre-health. I am always someone who turns to others for support and I believe that others in MED can turn to me for support as well. Having a community of support is helpful and inspiring when we are all pushing ourselves to do these stressful things. I am also very organized. If one of the members were to need something, I am likely to know exactly where it is or how to help them. I will always show up on time because I have my days planned out to almost the minute. One trait I can bring to MED is kindness. I genuinely love to help others and am always willing to go out of my way for the people around me. MED members who look out for one another and help each other is how the community that everyone loves is built.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: I have nannied ever since I was a freshman in high school. Although it is not the typical pre-health track job, it has taught me so much about how to care for others, even if they are small children. It has prepared me to be extremely patient and communicate with children who sometimes like patients, are unable to communicate their needs on a level that you are used to understanding. Sometimes you have to read their minds or communicate differently than what you are used too because they may be too stubborn to admit they need help or just unable to speak in general, like a 3 month old baby. I volunteered in my local hospital's infusion unit all summer. This was my first face-to-face healthcare experience. I got to communicate directly with patients and the nurses. I typically saw the same patients every week and got to see their treatment plan first-hand over the summer months. Most importantly, I learned how small gestures can make someone's day or even distract them from the long hours of treatment they have to go through. Back home in IL, I would always help my father on the farm. My father and my grandfather are the reason why I know what hard work is. My father never thought twice about not having a son, he allowed my sister and I to do the same work he was doing and never once questioned if we were incapable just because we were girls. I feel as if, even today their are still patients out there who want to see a male doctor and although that is tough to hear, I know for absolute sure women are amazing doctors too. Working on the farm also showed me that things have to be done even when it is not necessarily convenient. A lot of healthcare career hours are not your typical 9-5, however, I am used to this because some things cannot wait on the farm, just as patients cannot wait around for care.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare

My experiences in shadowing, volunteering, pursuing my CNA certification, and working as a manager have all helped prepare me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare.

As a whole these experiences have helped me understand that healthcare truly is being a voice for those who are unable to be heard.

candidates.name: Analei Frank

facts: Familiar with a current brother: Ruhi Shah, friend; Syd Nguyen, friend

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: When I chose the Allied Health major, at first, I based it on what I believed I was good at in high school. After finishing my AP Biology course, I realized I wanted to pursue healthcare. With a talk with a few members of my family, I landed on the Physician Assistant profession. Coming into school with a set plan and path ahead of me made me feel prepared for the journey ahead. I knew that this major would require an immense amount of studying and work, and I was really able to see that after starting my first semester at the University of Tampa in the Fall of 2025. The summer following, I was given the opportunity to intern at Cooper University Hospital. Here, I saw many of the happenings in the hospital as well as in outpatient clinics. This experience made me really fall in love with the profession. As I walked through the halls with the physician assistants I shadowed, I understood more about why they chose this profession. They were able to mentor me and gave me snippets of the journey they took to becoming a physician assistant. With this new understanding, I was able to figure out that physician assistants have a much more flexible work schedule compared to others in the medical field. Seeing patients and using the knowledge that I gained to help other people was something I loved. I found myself boasting about my experiences and what I was learning to my family at the end of the day. I loved the accomplished feeling of taking care of patients, learning why they came in, pinpointing the source, and making the diagnosis, as well as seeing the sometimes instant relief they felt from treatments.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: From MED, I hope to gain a community of people who can push each other to be the best they can, gain opportunities to volunteer in the Tampa community, and find people who share the same diligence and similar career path as me. Coming to the University of Tampa has made me realize that not everyone has the same goals as I do, and that can sometimes lead to having a more difficult time focusing and staying on track. Through this club, I hope to gain resources and friendships that will allow me to enhance my learning experience as well as my own social circle of people with similar interests and virtues as I do. By fostering friendships, I hope to also be able to give back to Tampa Bay as well as build my volunteering hours that are required for my Leadership Minor as well as hours for my physician’s assistant application. I feel that, if possible, everyone should try to give back to the community they live in to increase everyone's value of living. I used to love volunteering at my local food bank with my friends, and I was also able to volunteer at Feeding Tampa Bay at the beginning of my Fall semester of 2025. These experiences made me appreciate the things that I have and the people who work to always give back.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: The characteristics that I feel I can bring to the table are my confidence, willingness to help others, and my dedication to becoming the best healthcare provider and person I can become. Through my confident nature, I can aid in fostering an inclusive environment and help myself as well as others get involved. From playing sports all my life, I have felt that I have always been on a sort of “stage,” which I felt could have increased not only my confidence but also my ability to work well with others. With sports being heavy on teamwork, I feel like I have a well-developed ability to collaborate with others and be open to all ideas. I have learned through these experiences when to admit when I am wrong, as well as how to build upon ideas. I love the feeling of being a part of something that is bigger than myself and coordinating efforts to build upon my own interests. With this, I have been able to excel in group projects as well as help not only myself succeed but the people around me too. Finally, after my summer shadowing physician assistants, I have felt an even greater passion for healthcare. I followed some amazing people in oncology and orthopedics, and they were amazing mentors. I learned so much about this, and we were able to see some very head-turning cases. Being a part of this has given me a greater feeling of accomplishment at the end of the day and made me extremely confident in my decision to pursue this career.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: The experiences that I know have helped and will continue to help me prepare for the responsibilities of healthcare have been the Principles of the Exceptional Learner Program that I was a part of in high school, being on Tampa’s Women’s Rowing team, and my shadowing opportunity over the summer. Through the Principles of the Exceptional Learner, I was able to work alongside many other peer mentors to assist in the learning of students with neurodiversities. The goal of the program was to educate people without intellectual disabilities about the differences and strengths of people who are neurodiverse and to bridge the gap between people with and without intellectual disabilities. The Principles of the Exceptional Learner Program helped me better understand students who are different and have given me the confidence to work in the future with neurodiverse individuals. It also made me more compassionate toward the things that make people different from societal expectations. With this, I have been a part of a research project over the summer. The collaboration and work that we have all done have increased my knowledge of the official research process as well as furthered my ability to work with others who are not physically in front of me, since many of the other people on the team have been in other states than me. Working on this has helped me understand the role that artificial intelligence has in multiple aspects of the work since we used “Rayyan” to assist in the paring down of resources to extract from. Lastly, rowing for five years with a multitude of different teams has helped me be able to adapt to new environments as well as accomplish shared goals on each of my teams. With athletics, many of the goals we have are to win, which in this case would be celebrating anyone’s successes in academics, job search, and acceptance in a post graduation education. This has helped me enhance my skills in learning good sportsmanship, teamwork, and perseverance.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose Allied Health with a concentration in Medical Sciences as my major because I felt that the curriculum provided by the University was best fit for my future career as a PA. I am drawn to the Pre-PA track because I am looking for a career that has a good work-life balance while also being able to participate un hands-on patient care. My interest in healthcare comes from wanting a career that is challenging but also meaningful. I enjoy learning about the human body and how different aspects of science translate into real patient care. At the same time, I know that having a successfully career in heath care requires more than just a strong academic background. It requires strong communication skills, empathy, teamwork, and the ability to remain calm in stressful environments, which are all traits that I believe I am very strong in. What excites me most about pursuing a career in healthcare is the countless opportunities it provides to build relationships with patients while working as part of a medical team. I want patients to feel comfortable asking questions and addressing their concerns with me, while also diagnosing and treating them. Choosing the Pre-PA track has given me a clear path for my future in terms of next steps. There is still a lot for me to learn until I can actually treat patients, but that is something that I am aware of and excited to work towards. I am passionate about healthcare because it combines my continued interest in science with my desire to work with people and make a meaningful difference in the world.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: One of the most important things that I am hoping to gain from MED is a community of people who I can surround myself with that understand the pressure and challenges that being a pre-health major brings. All pre-health majors are very demanding, so having a solidified group of people to go to that understand what I am going through is very important to me. Beyond the scope of creating a community, I am also hoping to gain various different clinical experiences that can help me understand more about the medical field in different settings. Throughout my summer I completed an internship at an internal medicine office which showed me how that field is ran and it only made me more intrigued about this field. I am hoping to gain more clinical exposures in the other fields and specialties of medicine so that I can further understand what a day to day life looks like. Another huge factor that I am hoping to gain from MED is networking. I believe that the relationships that I can create through MED are going to matter a lot in the future. I want to be able to create connections with not only my fellow Utampa students, but other people in the medical field. I want to connect with people who will give me their honest advice, leading me in the correct path for the future. Most of all though, I am hoping to build friendships that will last my entire lifetime. Even though college is only four years of my life, I want to build strong bonds with my peers that will go beyond college. I want to create relationships with people who are going to lift me up, celebrate my wins, go to if things get hard, and I want to be able to reciprocate these things with them as well.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: One of the biggest strengths I bring to the table is strong communication skills. At the beginning of this semester, I was a Week Of Welcome Leader, helping the incoming freshmen and their families navigate throughout a completely new environment, the universities campus. During this time, I explain university resources and helped incoming students and their families feel welcomed and at home during the move-in process. I also strengthened my communication skills this summer through my internship where I communicated directly with patients about their symptoms and relay information back to them. Another skill that I is leadership. Through my role as a Week of Welcome leader and various positions  in high school, I have created opportunities to take initiative and guide others. I hold myself to very high standards in everything, always putting my best efforts towards the task at hand. Having played sports my entire life, teamwork has taught me how to communicate under pressure, support those around me, and put my ago aside. This mindset is something I would bring to MED. I do not just want to benefit from this organization, I want to actively support others involved in the organization. Above all, I am a very dedicated person. Whether it is academics, leadership, or my internship, I consistently put my best effort forward and follow through on my commitments. I believe  a strong work ethic is an important quality in the pre-health community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: This past summer, I completed an internship under Dr. Robert J. Laudicino, an MD who practices internal medicine and OB/GYN. Shadowing him gave me exposure to clinical procedures and how a medical office runs on a day-to-day basis. I experienced various patient interactions, communication between the staff, and the pace of the office. This internship also showed me how flexible a career in medicine can be, which helped me confirm that this is the field I want to pursue in the future. Being in that environment taught me things that no class could ever teach me. It taught me how to remain calm in a fast-paced environment, how to communicate with patients, and how much trust matters in the clinic. My role as a Week of Welcome leader also shaped me in an equally important way. I was responsible for helping incoming freshmen move in and adjust to this brand-new environment while they were stressed and overwhelmed. I had to communicate clearly and make people feel supported during this very big change in their lives. This experience has helped me prepare for a career in healthcare because a huge part of medicine is getting people during difficult times in their lives making them feel calm and cared for. I learned how to adjust my approach based on what they needed in that moment and how to stay calm when things were overwhelming. Together, these two experiences gave me both clinical exposure and a strong foundation in the skills that healthcare demands. My internship showed me the technical and professional side of medicine, while my role as a Week of Welcome leader strengthened my communication and composure. Being involved in student government and various pre-health organizations has kept me engaged with my peers who share the same goals and challenges.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose my major somewhat by chance. When I first started college, I was unsure of what I wanted to pursue, and I ultimately landed on biochemistry. As I have grown through my first year of college, I have learned to take my academic and professional path more seriously and have gradually become more passionate about pursuing the pre-med track. What started as an uncertain choice has developed into a career path that I genuinely see myself pursuing. My interest in anesthesiology began when I had the opportunity to shadow an anesthesiologist. Being in an operating room for the first time was an eye-opening experience. I was fascinated by the combination of science, decision-making, and patient care involved in anesthesia. As I continued shadowing in a larger hospital setting, my interest only grew. Seeing anesthesiologists work alongside surgeons, nurses, and other healthcare professionals showed me how important communication, precision, and teamwork are in providing safe patient care. What makes me passionate about healthcare is the opportunity to combine my interest in science with meaningful interactions with people. I am drawn to a career where I can continuously learn, work as part of a team, and make a direct difference in someone's experience during an important and often vulnerable moment in their life. My experiences so far have helped me realize that healthcare is not simply a career I am considering, but a field I genuinely want to grow in.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Through MED, I hope to gain a deeper understanding of what it means to pursue a career in healthcare and to become more confident in my path toward medical school. As a student who is still early in my college journey, I know there is so much I have yet to learn about medicine, the healthcare field, and the process of becoming a physician. I am especially excited to gain exposure to different areas of medicine and learn from professionals who can share their experiences and perspectives. My experiences shadowing anesthesiologists have sparked a strong interest in anesthesiology, but I also want to remain open-minded and explore the many opportunities within healthcare. I hope MED will allow me to better understand the realities of different medical careers and help me determine how my interests and strengths can translate into my future profession. Beyond career exploration, I hope to develop meaningful connections with other students who share my passion for healthcare and learn from mentors who can guide me throughout my undergraduate experience. I also want to strengthen my communication, leadership, and professional skills while gaining experiences that will prepare me for the responsibilities of working with patients. Ultimately, I hope to leave MED with a clearer sense of direction, a stronger foundation for my future in medicine, and a greater understanding of the kind of physician I hope to become.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I believe I would contribute curiosity, determination, adaptability, and a genuine willingness to learn to MED. As someone who is still early in my college journey, I recognize that I do not have all the answers yet, but I am not afraid to ask questions, seek out new experiences, and challenge myself to grow. My experiences in college have taught me that being willing to learn and improve is just as important as what I already know. I am also a hardworking and determined person. Pursuing a career in medicine requires commitment and perseverance, and I have learned to continue pushing myself even when coursework or new experiences feel challenging. I believe this determination would allow me to fully engage with the opportunities MED provides. Communication and teamwork are also skills I value. Through working with others in academic and professional settings, I have learned the importance of listening to different perspectives, communicating respectfully, and contributing to a team. These qualities are especially important in healthcare, where collaboration and clear communication directly impact patient care. Most importantly, I would bring an open mind and a genuine passion for learning about healthcare. I am eager to learn from mentors and other students while also sharing my own experiences and perspectives. I hope to contribute to MED not only by participating, but by being someone who is engaged, supportive, and willing to grow alongside the people around me.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences in college, along with my opportunities to explore healthcare, have helped me develop skills that I believe will prepare me for a career in medicine. Through shadowing physicians, I have gained a firsthand understanding of the professionalism, communication, and attention to detail required in a healthcare environment. My first experience shadowing an anesthesiologist allowed me to observe an operating room and see how physicians must remain focused, make thoughtful decisions, and work closely with an entire healthcare team. Continuing to shadow in a larger hospital setting further showed me how important collaboration and communication are to providing effective patient care. My academic experiences have also strengthened my ability to manage responsibilities and persevere through challenges. As a biochemistry student pursuing the pre-med track, I have learned that success requires consistency, time management, and a willingness to ask questions when I do not understand something. These are qualities I know will continue to be important as I take on the demanding coursework and responsibilities associated with a career in healthcare. Most importantly, my experiences have helped me become more comfortable learning from others and stepping outside of my comfort zone. Healthcare requires individuals who can adapt, communicate with people from different backgrounds, and remain compassionate while handling responsibility. My experiences so far have given me a foundation in these qualities and have strengthened my desire to continue gaining hands-on experiences that will prepare me to care for patients in the future.

I also love that dentistry is a career where there is always more to learn. Whether that means specializing in a certain field or taking additional courses to expand your skills and learn new techniques, there are always opportunities to grow. I try to be someone others can rely on, whether that means listening, helping someone through a stressful situation, or simply being there when needed. I think that mindset would allow me to contribute positively to MED and support the people around me.
I would also love the opportunity to grow within the organization, learn from other members, and continue developing both personally and professionally. I hope to contribute to MED while also becoming a better person, friend, and future healthcare professional.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
One of the experiences that prepared me most for a career in healthcare was a mission trip to Greece, where I volunteered as a dental assistant and helped provide dental care to people who did not always have the means or access to receive it. During the trip, we visited refugee shelters and worked with children to teach them about the importance of oral health and proper dental hygiene.
Seeing these different experiences gave me a unique perspective and a greater appreciation for the access to healthcare that many of us can take for granted. It showed me that healthcare is not only about treating a problem, but also about education, prevention, and making patients feel cared for and respected.
Outside of healthcare, I have also worked in several different environments, including lifeguarding, retail, and the food industry as a server. Each of these jobs has exposed me to people from different backgrounds and personalities and taught me how to communicate, adapt, and handle different situations.
Together, these experiences have shaped me to become more patient and understanding of the people we may come across. I believe those skills will be extremely important in healthcare, where every patient and situation presents something different.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose my Allied Health major and professional track because I have always been interested in how the human body works and, from a young age, have always been someone who wants to help and provide care. My interest became stronger through my experiences in HOSA and my Medical Seminar course in high school, where I studied human anatomy and organ systems and practiced suturing. Most notably, when I became a Health Literacy Ambassador for HOSA, I delivered a series of two presentations about skin cancer and SPF using case studies. When I was given the opportunity to choose any topic I wanted to present, I took inspiration from my background caring for my dad and grandmother, who had skin cancer, as well as my mom, who is a facial specialist. I wanted to share the science behind these two concepts while also informing my audience about the dangers of skin cancer and the benefits of SPF. This experience is a major reason why I am so passionate about dermatology and ultimately becoming a PA in this field. 

I want to work alongside doctors while also having the opportunity to connect with more individuals and provide care that not only addresses their medical concerns but also extends into their personal lives. I want to be empathetic toward patients and their skin concerns because of my own experience helping my dad and grandmother through their treatment and healing processes. 

My passion for healthcare also comes from my interest in cancer prevention and treatment. Through HOSA, I competed in Pharmacology and Nutrition, volunteered by creating care packages for breast cancer patients, and helped coordinate cancer-related events. I also volunteered at Moffitt Cancer Center, where I assisted nurses and receptionists with daily tasks and saw how many different people work together to care for patients.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
I hope to gain valuable connections and experiences through MED that can help me grow as a future healthcare professional. I hope to meet many people who share my interest in healthcare, as well as healthcare professionals who can provide insight and guidance from their own experiences.

I am also hoping to learn about internship and other professional opportunities that I may not be able to find on my own. Since I am looking into studying abroad in Spain next fall, I wold like to connect with professionals who have participated in studying abroad related to healthcare. Similarly, it would be beneficial to meet individuals that I could shadow, which would be incredible. This would be true, especially in other areas, such as Ophthalmology, Otolaryngology, and Allergy so that I can identify if I may have other areas that I could be interested in.

Academic resources is another element that can positively influence my future if I am a part of MED. As most know, I will have to take the PA-CAT exam to enter PA school and then the PANCE exam to become certified once I am in graduate school. I hope to seek out the academic resources that MED offers so I can prepare myself early for these exams. 

Most importantly, I want to use MED as an opportunity to build relationships with people who can help me learn and grow. I hope these connections and experiences will be valuable and will last, helping me become more confident and prepare me for future opportunities in the field.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
I believe my leadership skills, communication, organization, and willingness to work with others would allow me to contribute to MED. Through my leadership roles in HOSA, Key Club, and NHS, I have learned how to take initiative, work with different people, and follow through with my responsibilities.

As a Vice President for Key Club and NHS, I consistently upheld a positive leadership role. When holding meetings, I always made sure to listen with an open mind and try to understand our members' perspectives and thoughts on potential event and donation ideas. I took charge respectfully in areas that were lacking and stepped up to the plate by organizing several blood drives. I worked from May through August to organize quarterly blood drives, while also providing free food for donors from local food truck vendors in the area. This ultimately led to the creation of a scholarship fund for my high school where every time someone donates blood on campus with OneBlood, the company will donate $10 to the school's fund. This experience taught me what it means to be a leader by taking charge when the opportunity is available while also accepting feedback and criticism openly from members and other officers in both clubs.

Through HOSA, I have also developed my ability to lead and work toward a common goal. As Treasurer, I helped organize fundraisers and chapter events, including a Drive-Through Snack Shack and Breakfast fundraiser that raised more than $1,000. I also competed in Nutrition and Pharmacology, placing fourth in my region and advancing to the state level.

I would bring these leadership experiences, along with an open mind, positive attitude, and determination to learn, to MED. I feel fulfilled when working with others and would use my skills to contribute to the MED community while bettering myself as a future healthcare professional.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences have taught me that working in healthcare takes a lot more than just being good at science. It takes patience, flexibility, and learning how to connect with people when they are vulnerable.

Volunteering at Moffitt Cancer Center gave me a great look into how a hospital runs. Doing tasks like answering call lights, restocking supplies, and keeping sanitation carts ready showed me that even the small jobs make a large difference for the nurses and patients. Answering call lights especially taught me how important it is to listen, respond quickly, and help calm a patient's anxiety when they're waiting to be cared for.

Through HOSA, competing in Pharmacology gave me a stronger grasp on the technical side of care, and making care packages for breast cancer patients reminded me of the human side. Healthcare extends beyond just diagnosing a problem, it's really about remembering what the patient is going through emotionally and taking that into account when treating them. Touching on my background again, I have truly learned to be empathetic when it comes to helping others. I believe it's essential to view someone's situation from not only your own perspective but theirs too. This skill will be very applicable to a career in healthcare as I will be able to connect with patients in a way that makes them feel seen and heard. 

Finally, working as a camp counselor and volunteering at food pantries forced me out of my comfort zone. Managing groups of kids required a lot of patience, and helping families at food pantries taught me how to treat every single person with respect, no matter their background. When I was appointed to be an assistant translator to the interns working at the food pantry, it not only gave me pride in the fact that I could assist them but it also gave me challenging experiences that I could work on navigating. For example, when a client that had already visited once in a week came back to receive food, I had to navigate difficult conversations to respectfully let them know that they wouldn't be served. As a result, experiences like those allowed me to communicate better as I learned to be flexible when dealing with all types of people even non-English speakers. This connects my future in healthcare as I will now be more confident when having challenging conversations with patients, especially if they speak Spanish.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
My drive to earn my MD/PhD in Neuropsychiatry stems from my own experience and a strong desire to help others avoid some of the struggles I went through. I was diagnosed with ADHD and dyslexia during the second half of high school, after more than a decade of being described as loud, unfocused, and disruptive. By then, I was barely holding a 2.5 GPA and had convinced myself that college probably wasn't going to happen for me.
I didn't understand that many of the things I had been taught to see as deficits were also connected to some of my greatest strengths. Dyslexia meant to me that I couldn't read well. I didn't know that the way my brain processed information also gave me strong pattern recognition, spatial reasoning, and a highly visual way of thinking. I wasn't worse at learning; I had been learning differently without knowing how to work with it.
That realization led me to neuropsychiatry. I spent the next two years teaching myself neuroscience, partly because I wanted to understand my own brain and partly because neuroscience finally gave me a framework that made my mind make sense instead of making me feel broken. When I was later reevaluated, my reading performance had improved enough that I no longer met the diagnostic criteria for dyslexia. I don't see that as something I was "fixed" from. Through understanding how my brain worked, I had developed compensatory pathways that I still rely on today.
That experience is what draws me to the intersection of psychiatry and neuroscience. I want to become a clinician-scientist who studies the complexity of learning disabilities, especially in Women, and works alongside them to help make their strengths known and developed, rather than simply naming a disorder and focusing on negatives or medications.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
Coming from a nontraditional academic background, a 2.5 GPA through most of high school, a late diagnosis, and no built-in network of doctors or scientists in my family, I haven't had much of the guidance many pre-health students have access to. I've also had a difficult time finding like-minded people, as you and I both know these aspirations require a lot of time and discipline. 
That's one of the biggest things I'm hoping to gain from MED: a community of people who are on a similar path, so we can support each other. I'm also looking for accountability and perspective. I've had to be very self-directed to get this far, teaching myself neuroscience, figuring out how to understand my own diagnosis, and building a business while keeping up with school. That independence has helped me, but it also means I've gotten used to working things out mostly on my own. I transferred and have 1 friend who is also pre-health. I take my dedication to the extreme, especially knowing how important my environment is, and I've gotten used to not prioritizing socialization so I don't get distracted or pulled back. I'm hoping to build a group of peers who genuinely want to see each other succeed and support one another through the long road ahead. Hearing everyone in the meeting and afterward speaking about their similar struggles with isolation due to this unique college experience brought me so much joy in knowing there are others who are going through this too, and there is a community I belong to; I just had not found it.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
One of the biggest things I would bring to MED is a genuinely insatiable curiosity. I am truly a nerd. I will research something because I want to understand it, and then somehow end up three hours later reading about a completely different mechanism that caught my attention along the way. I genuinely love learning, but more than that, I love science and understanding why things work.
Much of my curiosity outside the classroom centers on learning itself. I spend all of my free time researching how people can learn, study, and function at their best, from the neuroscience of studying and memory to nutrition and other factors that affect cognition and performance. I turn much of what I learn into educational social media content, which has also taught me how to take complicated information and make it interesting and useful for people without a scientific background. I would love to bring that curiosity and science communication to MED as well.
I also bring a lot of energy and high standards for myself. I care deeply about what I commit to and push myself to genuinely understand something rather than just get through it. At the same time, I'm not interested in making everything serious. I love meeting new people, getting excited about ideas together, and having fun with people who are equally passionate. I think a good community needs both ambition and people who make the experience enjoyable.
I also value finding people who understand parts of my experience without needing a long explanation. I don't drink at all, and I've learned firsthand that even choices that are completely comfortable for you can feel isolating when you don't have many people around you who share them. I was told some MED members don't drink either, and that immediately stood out to me. I would love to contribute to a community where people can be ambitious, curious, and still feel like they belong.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My path to medicine has looked different from the traditional pre-med path. I have been working two jobs since I was 17, and for the first three years of college, I continued working as an Events Director for four years while also serving and carrying my coursework. I have had to prioritize working because I have been responsible for paying my own bills and, until now, much of my education. I had less time than many students to pursue traditional pre-med experiences; it taught me responsibility in a very real way.
Working in events taught me to stay organized when many people depend on me, communicate under pressure, handle problems when things don't go as planned, and follow through even when I am exhausted. Serving has added another dimension: paying attention to what people need, adapting quickly, and learning how to make someone feel heard and cared for even when I cannot give them exactly what they want.
Outside of school, I also mentor students with learning differences similar to my own. I understand the frustration of feeling like everyone else seems to know how to learn except you, and I enjoy helping students find strategies that work with their brains rather than against them. I have also nannied for a family with three children with Fragile X syndrome, which taught me patience, flexibility, and how much communication can matter when working with children who have different needs.
More recently, I joined a research lab under a professor, an important step toward building the scientific experience I want for my future in medicine.
I know my resume may not look exactly like that of a traditional pre-med student. But I am now in a position to dedicate more time to medicine, research, and service, and I am fully committed to doing so. I am intentionally making this the next priority in my education, and I see MED as an important part of building the experiences, mentorship, and community I need to prepare for medical school.

There is always a demand for nurses and though I’m not quite certain what branch of nursing I’m committed to yet, I know that there will always be space and an opportunity for any kind of nurse. Nursing also is one of those careers that I can further my education and explore different departments which I am interested in. I like knowing that my career is going to make an impact on someone's life just by doing my job, and though it is definitely hard work I know the hard work pays off by being able to help others.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare

I liked the idea of not having to stick to a certain specialty for my entire life, so the PA path started to interest me more, as you have more freedom and you can change specialities throughout your career. Another factor that attracted me to the PA path was the financial stability that comes with it. notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

It would also help me get hours for my application for PA school. To be a competitive applicant, it is important to have thousands of hours, and MED provides many opportunities to get that.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring

I think I am very friendly, communicative, and personable which can help me connect with others in MED. I like to make friends and connections, and I love talking to people. I think I am also very dependable and hard working. I take all my commitments very seriously, and put my best efforts into them. I would definitely be very committed to MED, as the people in it are very like-minded and have similar goals as me. I like to think that I am very open-minded as well, and I am always willing to hear from other people. From all of my commitments in the past, I think I have gained the skill of being very reliable. I have learned how to take initiative and handle responsibilities without the guidance of someone else. Overall, I believe my reliability, communication skills, responsibility, hardworking nature, and willingness to connect with others would contribute to MED and help me be an active and positive member.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: The jobs I have had along with extracurricular activities and volunteer work have really inspired me and opened me up to the healthcare world. I have worked in childcare ever since I was 16, and I have been babysitting for years before that as well. One thing that I think has really prepared me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare was working with special needs kids. While I was a camp counselor, I was assigned to a special needs children, and I was one-on-one with them. I was responsible for that child and I had to pay attention to that child’s specific needs and individual behaviors. This taught me patience, empathy, and understanding. I also have been babysitting for a number of years and different families, including here in Tampa. Babysitting has taught me independence and accountability. It has made me a more responsible person, communicate effectively, and make responsible decisions. Additionally, I think that growing up and playing sports has also prepared me for the responsibilities in healthcare, as I have been part of a team throughout my entire life.
