notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose to major in Allied Health, with a concentration in Medical Sciences, because I knew it was the most effective route to pursue my passion for Anesthesia. I am drawn to the precision aspect of Anesthesia and the vigilance that is required. As a student currently in an Anatomy and Physiology course, I am learning about the nervous system, which I find intriguing. Understanding how the body responds to medication and intervention during vulnerable real-life situations is truly captivating. I am especially passionate about the close relationship between Anesthesia and neuroscience. I find the responsibility of making quick decisions, adjusting each dosage and procedure for each patient, very inspiring. I admire the team aspect as well, which encourages constant communication, adaptability, and problem-solving. Recently, I had the opportunity to shadow an Anesthesiologist and be a spectator in the operating room. I learned about the interscalene nerve block, a regional nerve block used to block shoulder pain signals during a shoulder arthroplasty, and about a few of the precise medications used, such as Propofol and Zofran. While I was in the operating room, surrounded by the Anesthesiologist and team of surgeons, I felt an adrenaline rush that made me feel fully capable of pursuing this career. It almost feels like you are solving a puzzle in somebody's life and are trying to find the "perfect pieces" or dosages, while someone's life is on the line.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I was attracted to Mu Epsilon Delta because of the drive that all of the students share towards building their careers in the healthcare field. I am hoping to gain lifelong connections with other students, regardless of what career path in medicine they are pursuing.  Additionally, I am hoping to gain volunteer experience and the opportunity to give back to the community. Beyond that, I'm hoping MED will provide mentorship from students who are further along in the pre-health process. As someone who just earned my CNA certification, I know there is still so much to learn about navigating this path. I want to learn from people because ultimately, that is how we all get better. I'm also hoping to grow as a leader, whether that be by helping organize events or supporting other members who are on a pre-health track as well. Ultimately, I see MED as a community that will challenge me to keep growing from both a personal and academic standpoint.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I bring relentless drive, tenacity, and ambition that would make me a strong addition to Mu Epsilon Delta. Balancing multiple extracurriculars, jobs, and schoolwork shows my ability to push forward toward long-term goals without losing momentum. That same drive led me to co-found a mental health awareness club at Align Wellness Center with a clinical psychologist. My ambition also shows in how I've sought out experience wherever I could find it, from volunteering with underprivileged children through Pass It Along to earning my CNA license before even graduating college. I see MED as a community that will push me to keep raising the bar and setting a high standard to keep the momentum towards my bright future.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My path toward healthcare has not been a linear one; however, they have all taught me insightful skills that will better prepare me to be a healthcare professional. As a lifeguard, I was taught constant vigilance and how to stay calm under pressure. Responding to real-life emergencies that could happen at any point in time was not an easy task, but it taught me the importance of composure, as well as AED and CPR use. Additionally, with my internship at the Align Wellness Center, I was connected to students with mental health illnesses, which taught me healthcare is more than just physical, but mental. Running community awareness events taught me about healthcare from a mental perspective more than ever in my life. To add to my experience working with students, I also had the opportunity to volunteer at Pass it Along, which allowed me to work with underprivileged children over multiple summers. This challenged me; however, it made me more adaptable, helped me connect with people from all different backgrounds, and find ways to make others feel safe, comfortable, and seen, which directly relates to serving diverse patients. Working in the hospitality industry improved my ability to respond to needs promptly in hectic environments and not to go off a script, but to adapt to different situations constantly. In addition, my CNA certification, which I recently received, will better prepare me by equipping me with a clinical foundation, whether that is taking vitals, providing patient hygiene, mobility assistance, or simply being a friend a person relies on on a day-to-day basis.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I originally wanted to become an orthopedic surgeon because of my own experience with bone problems while running track in high school. However, after shadowing an orthopedic surgeon, I realized that the day-to-day responsibilities of the profession were not the right fit for me. This realization led me to change my major to Allied Health and declare a Pre-Medical Sciences concentration with the goal of PA school. After shadowing a physician assistant, I found that the environment, patient interaction, and day-to-day responsibilities were much more aligned with what I envisioned for myself. I was fortunate to babysit for a healthcare professional in a leadership position at Inspira, a major hospital system in my area. She had told me that with my connections and future goals for undergraduate school, getting into a PA school would be more than doable. Ultimately, I decided to put my ego aside and step down from the path to an MD, and instead focus on myself and what I wanted for my life, which is perfectly fit for a PA.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: The two biggest things for me when it comes to joining MED are community and resources. Through meeting people already in the fraternity, I realized I had been lacking something like MED for a while. All of my friends are business and criminal justice majors, so studying with people and talking about career paths really never came up. When I ran into Stefani while studying for our Bio 2 final, I learned about the fraternity and started to like the idea of being able to study and talk with others in my field more often. You guys seem like a super cool group of people with a lot in common, and I would love to be a part of that circle. I am also really interested in all of the resources the fraternity has to offer. The biggest one is research opportunities, which I have desperately been trying to be a part of since attending the University of Tampa. Being able to have exclusive opportunities to be a part of those labs is a dream come true, and one of the biggest unchecked boxes on my undergrad wishlist. I'm currently volunteering in one now as a test subject, with hopes that the professor likes me enough to bring me on to her team. I also really like the volunteer opportunities you offer. As someone going into healthcare, my biggest concern is helping people. For example, I love giving to the homeless in the city with my extra swipes, and doing the volunteer work offered through you guys would be another great way to give back to the community. I always want to do volunteer work, but I can never seem to find any openings.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I have a couple of good traits, such as social skills, study habits, and networking. Firstly, I believe my personality would fit right in with the brothers. I tend to get along with everyone in my science classes, and I would assume the same when it comes to most members of the fraternity. I also enjoy studying with partners or groups. With that, I would love to get into study groups with like-minded people in the same classes as me and offer help + discuss the material so we can all get a better understanding. Another thing I do really well is networking. I've done a great job so far of building my network of professors and professionals, and I believe that, with the support and resources of MED, I would be able to continue to do so, weaving those into the fraternity and creating more opportunities throughout the frat for current and future members.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: With shadowing experiences in various work environments such as Physical Therapy, Physician, and Physician Assistant, I have started to grasp a solid foundation of how the healthcare field works. They keep things very organized and professional and also tend to know their stuff very well. These experiences enlightened me to take my undergraduate studies as seriously as possible, making sure to drill all of the material into my brain to ensure a seamless transition into the profession. But I've done a lot more than shadow and assist healthcare professionals. I would first like to talk about my experience as a soccer referee. When refereeing children's soccer, it's very important to stand strong in high-speed and high-stress environments. People running and screaming when calls are made is normal, and your job as a referee is to stay calm during these experiences and deliver appropriate responses to every situation. I also managed a boba stand at a very popular asian festival located here in Tampa. The festival was 3 days long, with 12-hour shifts that gave no breaks. Aside from all of the duties of a normal worker, I was also tasked with implementing systems to ensure a smooth run throughout these busy days. Doing things like maximizing efficiency when it came to making drinks, creating an organized ordering system, and handling specific customer requests all came with the job as the manager. I learned leadership and problem-solving over those 3 days, which are very applicable to the healthcare field. Additionally, I do babysitting for a family back home. Watching these kids through the years has taught me how to take care of people, listen, respond in appropriate ways to ensure compliance, and bond with them. If you're working with someone for long periods of time, the process is much more enjoyable when you grow a connection with them, as I've learned through babysitting. All of these lessons were extremely important and will be applied to how I operate in the medical field.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
Growing up, I always knew that I wanted to become a doctor. I think it was watching Grey's Anatomy. However, it wasn't until my sophomore year of high school that my true passion for healthcare took flight. I got my first job as a cashier at a local pharmacy. I became fascinated by how medications could interact with the body and treat illnesses. I found myself curious about how all the different drugs work and wanting to learn more.

My interest grew even further when I earned my pharmacy technician license and was allowed to be able to fill prescriptions. Being able to take on that responsibility gave me a small idea about what it would be like to be a pharmacist, and I was immediately hooked. I realized that pharmacy is something I could do for the rest of my life, and with my combined interest in healthcare, I knew that being a pharmacist was what I wanted.

What I'm most passionate about in healthcare is how the pharmacy field is constantly changing. It fascinates me how bacteria/disease can develop resistance to our medications, but then scientists develop new drugs. I love the idea of always being able to learn something new and the fact that, unfortunately, there will be someone who needs help. However, I want to be able to figure out if there is something out there that can help them. I'm good at problem-solving and connecting to people. I know deep down this career is for me.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I hope to gain most from MED is the community. I would love to grow connections with people who share my passion for healthcare. I believe that the most valuable opportunities in college come from the connections we make with other people. I want to meet students from different healthcare tracks and see what drives them in their fields. I'd love to build a network of people who can support me throughout my journey. I also hope to connect with professionals and alumni who can provide insight from their experiences.

As a pre-pharmacy student, I have noticed that there are not a lot of students at our school pursuing pharmacy compared to other healthcare professions. Because of this, I have found it difficult to know where to begin. I've had to look for advice and opportunities by myself. I'd love for MED to help me make connections, but I also want to be a resource for other pre-pharmacy students who may be feeling as lost as I was.

Ultimately, I hope that MED will allow me to grow personally and professionally while also providing me with the opportunity to meet people with whom I wouldn't have been able to.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
One of the biggest traits I would contribute to MED is my determination. I am not the type of person to give up on my goals. If there is something I want to get done, I get it done. Even if that means I need to step out of my comfort zone.

One example of this is the effort I have put into building connections within the pharmacy field. I have been able to connect with professors at the University of Florida when I went to the Pre-Pharmacy Student Conference, the chairman of the pharmacy program at the University of South Florida through Dr. Kalpana Makhijani, and Chris Christopoulos, the Senior District Pharmacy Supervisor for Walgreens in the St. Petersburg area. These connections happened because I put myself in the spotlight. I confidently communicated my goals and interest in pharmacy. I believe this demonstrates my initiative and how serious I am.

I would be able to contribute my strong communication skills to MED. I genuinely enjoy meeting new people, and I believe I can use those skills to help create an environment where members feel comfortable connecting with one another.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences working in a pharmacy and pursuing my pharmacy technician license have given me a strong foundation for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare. From what I've previously said, when I was a sophomore in high school, I started working as a cashier at a local pharmacy. What began as a simple job quickly became something that changed the direction of my future. Being around medications and seeing how they help patients really sparked my curiosity about how drugs interact with the human body.

As I became more interested in pharmacy, I earned my pharmacy technician license and was given the responsibility of filling and dispensing prescriptions. This experience gave me a small glimpse into what it would be like to work as a pharmacist.

My experiences have also helped me become more comfortable connecting with people. I have actively sought out opportunities to learn more about pharmacy by attending conferences and connecting with professors from different universities. I believe that persistence and a willingness to learn are qualities that will help me succeed in a career dedicated to caring for others.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I knew I wanted to go into healthcare because I wanted a career where I would be working with people and doing something different every day rather than sitting behind a desk. Having meaningful interactions and being able to do something different each day is really important to me. I have also always enjoyed learning in a hands-on way, and I don’t want that to stop once I earn my degree. I want to continue learning and working hands-on throughout my career. Healthcare is constantly changing, which means there will always be something new to learn. I don’t want to get caught in a cycle where everything feels repetitive, so having a career with new advancements, challenges, and patients is something that really appeals to me.

This was important to me when choosing a career path, and seeing my aunt, who is an X-ray technologist, have different experiences and stories with patients each week made me realize that healthcare was something I wanted to explore further. Although radiology ultimately wasn’t the path for me, it introduced me to the many different careers within healthcare. Coming into college, I thought I wanted to become a physician assistant, but as I learned more about the profession, I started to feel like I was choosing it partly because it was a common path for students interested in healthcare. After doing more research, I discovered the less commonly known path of becoming a Certified Anesthesiologist Assistant. The more I learned about it, the more I realized it combined everything I was looking for. It involves patient interaction, hands-on work, continuous learning, and a career that I am genuinely excited about.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I’m hoping to gain from MED is the opportunity to meet new people and find a group that I can really connect with and relate to. I want to meet students who are also serious about healthcare and have similar goals to me, so I can surround myself with people who are driven, passionate, and motivated. I really believe that the people you surround yourself with can have a big influence on you, and I want to be around people who push me to become better and stay motivated toward my goals, both in healthcare and in general.

I also want to get more involved. I took my freshman year to adjust to college life and figure out how to best thrive here, but now I’m ready to put my energy and drive into an organization, and I hope it can be MED. Being part of MED would give me the chance to learn from older students who have already gone through some of the same things I’m experiencing and can offer advice about classes, applications, and healthcare experiences. Since CAA is a less common career path, I would especially value meeting people who share similar interests or have experiences that could help me learn more. I also hope to find opportunities through MED to volunteer, shadow, and become more involved with the healthcare community in Tampa. I know these experiences will be important as I work toward becoming a CAA, and I want to start gaining them now. I am also a good listener and make an effort to hear other people out. I think this has helped me become a better communicator and work well with others. notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My jobs and extracurricular experiences have given me a lot of experience working with and being responsible for other people. I was a gymnastics coach for several years, which taught me how to work with people who have different personalities, learning styles, and comfort levels. Not everyone responds to the same instructions or encouragement, so I learned how to adjust the way I communicated depending on who I was working with. I also had to pay close attention to safety, especially when teaching new skills, and learned how important it is to stay focused and responsible when other people are depending on you.
Nannying has taught me many of these same things in a different way. Being responsible for a child meant that I had to be dependable, aware of what was going on around me, and able to make decisions on my own. I also had to communicate with both the child and her parents and adjust when plans did not go as expected. I think learning how to handle different situations while staying patient and responsible will be valuable in healthcare, where every patient and situation can be different.

In high school, I was also involved in National Honor Society, Science NHS, Math NHS, and Student Government. Being involved in several different organizations taught me how to manage my time, work with different groups of people, and contribute when I was needed. These experiences have made me more comfortable working with others and taking on responsibilities rather than waiting for someone else to do them. I know a career in healthcare will require me to work closely with many different people and take my responsibilities seriously. My experiences have helped me become a better communicator, more adaptable, and more comfortable being responsible for others. I believe these are skills I can continue to build on as I work toward becoming a CAA.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose Biology because I genuinely do enjoy learning about the natural world, particularly the human body and ecosystems. I want to become a physician because practicing medicine would allow me to apply my interest in the human body while building meaningful connections with the people I care for. 

I’m also a big-picture thinker, and to me, it’s not enough to only treat someone once they arrive at a hospital. I want to understand what caused them to become sick, what could have prevented it, and what happens after they leave. This is why I’m also interested in public health and hope to pursue an MD/MPH. I want to combine caring for individual patients with understanding and improving the larger systems that influence their health. 

My international background has especially shaped this interest. I have not only spoken with people from different countries about their healthcare systems, but have also experienced different systems myself, especially growing up in Namibia. This has made me more aware of how different people can experience healthcare depending on where they live and what resources they have. 

On top of this the world is developing so quickly, especially in AI, and healthcare with it. I want to be part of that transformation while helping make sure as few people as possible are left behind.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I hope to gain most from MED is simply being surrounded by like-minded people who are working towards similar goals. I’ve learnt that the pre-health path is very demanding, and I think there is a lot of value in having a community of people who understand that experience and can support and learn from each other. 

I am also looking for guidance from people who are further along the same path as me. I think there’s only so much you can learn from researching things on your own, and I would really value being able to learn from members who have already experienced the classes, clinical opportunities, volunteering, research, and other challenges that I will encounter throughout my undergraduate career. I think having that kind of guidance would help me grow both personally and professionally. 

Of course, I’m super excited about the connections, volunteering, and other opportunities that come with being part of MED, but I see those as things that naturally come from being actively involved in a strong community. 

Eventually, I would also like to give that guidance back. As I become an upperclassman and gain more experience myself, I hope I can become someone younger members can come to for advice and support.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare

Through volunteering in shelters and other community settings, I have interacted with people from different backgrounds and learned the importance of approaching people without assumptions and treating everyone with respect. Balancing these responsibilities with school and extracurriculars has strengthened my time management, communication, and ability to work with others. While these experiences don’t replicate working with patients, they have taught me how to be accountable to other people, which I believe is an important foundation for a career in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
My interest in healthcare began when I was young after needing stitches in my head. Although it was a stressful experience, I remember being fascinated by the person who was able to help me feel better and leave feeling confident that I was okay, and that my face wasn't ruined. From that moment, I became drawn to the idea of becoming a healthcare provider who could help people feel their best, both physically and emotionally.

As I grew older, my own experiences with healthcare deepened that interest. After struggling with symptoms for years, I was diagnosed with PCOS. Navigating those symptoms, my body gave me a personal understanding of how frustrating it can be to feel like something is wrong without having answers. It also showed me how important it is for healthcare providers to listen to their patients and take concerns seriously.

These experiences led me to pursue Allied Health with a concentration in Medical Sciences on the Pre-PA track. I am especially interested in dermatology and women’s health, conditions like PCOS, where I believe there is still much to learn and improve through research, education, and patient-centered care.

My passion for healthcare comes from wanting to combine science with genuine human connection. I hope to become a PA who not only treats patients, but also makes them feel heard, supported, and confident in their care while contributing to solutions that can improve healthcare more broadly.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What initially drew me to Mu Epsilon Delta was the sense of community I saw through the organization’s social media and tabling events. The members seemed to have a genuine bond while also being motivated, hardworking, and serious about their futures in healthcare. That combination stood out to me because I believe the people you surround yourself with in college can have a major influence on who you become.

Through MED, I hope to build relationships with students who share my passion for healthcare while learning from people with different interests and experiences. I want to be surrounded by individuals who challenge me to grow academically, professionally, and personally, while also having a community that celebrates each other’s accomplishments and supports one another through challenges.

I am also hoping to gain a better understanding of the many paths within healthcare. As a Pre-PA student, I am still developing my professional identity, and I would value the opportunity to learn from members who have already gained clinical, volunteer, research, and leadership experiences.

Most importantly, I want to contribute to MED rather than simply benefit from being a member. I would love to bring my interests in women’s health, dermatology, patient advocacy, and research to the organization while participating in service and supporting my fellow members. I see MED as a community where I can grow alongside people who are equally committed to making a difference in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
I believe I would contribute to MED through my empathy, willingness to learn, reliability, and genuine desire to care for others. I have always been someone who enjoys taking care of the people around me, which is one reason I have babysat for many years. Although babysitting is very different from working in healthcare, it has taught me patience, responsibility, adaptability, and how important it is to make people feel safe and comfortable in my care.

My experiences volunteering with Interact have also strengthened my ability to serve others. Working with children with special needs and older adults taught me that helping someone does not always require a major action. Sometimes, it means being patient, paying attention to what someone needs, and being willing to help with something that may be difficult for them.

I would also bring curiosity and a strong willingness to learn. My interest in healthcare extends beyond becoming a PA; I am genuinely interested in understanding why health disparities exist and how research and innovation can improve patient outcomes, particularly in women’s health.

Finally, I value collaboration. I want to be someone who celebrates the successes of others, offers support when someone is struggling, and contributes wherever I can. I believe these qualities would allow me to build meaningful relationships within MED while contributing positively to the organization and its mission.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences working, volunteering, and becoming involved in pre-health organizations have helped me develop many of the qualities I believe are essential in healthcare: patience, responsibility, communication, empathy, and the ability to care for people with different needs.

I have babysat for many years, and while it may not be a traditional healthcare experience, it has taught me a great deal about responsibility and caregiving. Being responsible for another person requires patience, attentiveness, adaptability, and the ability to remain calm when situations do not go as planned. Most importantly, babysitting has reinforced something I have always enjoyed: taking care of others and knowing that I can make someone feel safe and supported.

Through Interact, I have also had opportunities to work with children with special needs and older adults, including helping with tasks that may be more difficult for them. These experiences taught me that meaningful service begins with recognizing what another person needs rather than assuming what is best for them. That perspective is something I hope to carry into my future career as a PA.

My dermatology shadowing experience gave me a different perspective by allowing me to observe healthcare from the provider’s side. I was surprised by how busy the dermatologist’s schedule was, with back-to-back patients throughout the day, yet she still developed a personal connection with each person. That experience showed me that being an effective healthcare provider requires both clinical knowledge and the ability to make patients feel genuinely cared for. I was also fascinated by seeing treatments such as PRP being used to promote hair growth, which reminded me how quickly medicine continues to evolve.

Finally, participating in pre-health clubs at the University of Tampa has given me opportunities to connect with like-minded students and seek out experiences that prepare me for a healthcare career. Together, these experiences have strengthened my desire to pursue medicine while teaching me that excellent healthcare requires both scientific curiosity and genuine compassion.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose anesthesia for a multitude of reasons, primarily the ability to remain with patients throughout their entire care. So much of medicine can feel rushed or fragmented, but anesthesia lets you stay right by their side—easing their nerves before surgery, keeping them safe during it, and guiding their recovery after. For me, it merges all my passions: pharmacology, physiology, and hands-on patient care. Beyond the reward of helping others, I love the ability to create visible change every day. While healthcare is demanding and mentally taxing, knowing you’re producing a better outcome for the patient makes it worth it. Through my work as a medical assistant and receptionist, I saw both sides of healthcare. I saw the sacrifices patients make logistically and financially just to get care, and being able to see their progression in real time was incredibly rewarding. I chose Allied Health because it provided the clearest pathway toward my goal of becoming an anesthesiologist assistant.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I hope to gain a community from MED that goes beyond my remaining years at Utampa. Being a STEM major can be overwhelming and lonely at times. Finding a community of driven, hardworking individuals that all have the common goal of helping others every day is a community I want to surround myself in. I hope to not only do my part in giving back to the community through volunteering but to form meaningful connections with other brothers.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
My interest in joining MED comes down to a few core traits: strong leadership, solid organization, and clear communication. Through the President’s Leadership Fellows program, I learned what real leadership looks like. It isn't just taking charge—it’s listening, bringing out the strengths in other people, and working together toward a shared goal.
In both school and healthcare, keeping things organized and communicating well is everything. Being able to manage complex schedules and heavy workloads helps me stay dependable and focused, even when things get stressful. On top of that, working directly with patients and being active on campus has taught me how to connect with all kinds of people with empathy and clarity. I’m excited to bring that same energy, reliability, and teamwork to the MED community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
Through my work as a medical assistant and receptionist, I have seen firsthand the effort, empathy, and adaptability it takes to deliver quality healthcare. Sitting at the front desk, I observed the financial, physical, and logistical sacrifices patients make just to be seen. That perspective transformed how I approached my role in the back as a medical assistant. I realized that direct care isn't just about taking vitals or completing clinical tasks; it is about managing patient anxiety and offering reassurance during vulnerable moments. Working in a fast-paced clinic taught me to stay organized, pivot quickly when emergencies arise, and communicate clearly under pressure.
	Beyond clinical work, my campus leadership roles have prepared me for the team dynamics of healthcare. As a SPEARs mentor, I managed a cohort of thirty freshmen, helping them navigate individual academic and personal goals while adjusting to college life. This experience honed my ability to listen actively, tailor my communication to different personalities, and support people through stressful transitions. Additionally, stepping up as president of the Pre-Anesthesiologist Assistant Club meant navigating how to run an executive board and lead a campus organization for the first time. I had to learn how to delegate effectively, coordinate logistics, and build a collaborative environment from the ground up.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: When I was a junior in high school, my second cousin was dog-sitting and was unfortunately attacked by that dog. As a result, she experienced an arm amputation above her elbow and damage to her face, obstructing both her vision and breathing. After many surgical operations and considerable time in physical therapy, she is able to thrive independently! After witnessing how greatly physical therapy changed her life and has allowed her to get back to her job and participate in her daughter’s life, I became inspired to pursue a job in physical therapy. However, I am more interested in becoming a pediatric physical therapist compared to other specialties, as I have significant experience working in childcare and have become very passionate about working with a younger age group. After deciding I wanted to study physical therapy, I found that the University of Tampa had a physical therapy concentration under the Allied Health major, and I found that the courses I would take under the major were of great interest to me and would strongly prepare me for graduate school. Broadly speaking, I find myself passionate about healthcare because I want to work directly with people and make an impact in their lives that benefits their day-to-day and supports them in being the healthiest and happiest version of themselves. By working as a physical therapist, assisting people in improving their daily acts of living can go underappreciated by the general population, but knowing that I am making a valuable change in an individual person’s life is truly what matters to me.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: If granted the opportunity to become a brother of Mu Epsilon Delta, I hope to find friendship in fellow students at the University of Tampa who are on a similar path as I am, who have a genuine interest in providing care to people and have the same drive and passion that I do. Many times our sciences classes that many of us are in together do not allow for us to truly meet all of our classmates and talk about our interests and professional goals outside of icebreakers, so being part of MED I believe would be an amazing opportunity to not only network, but grow close with the brothers and recognize more faces in our classes. Already taking academically challenging courses is difficult enough, but not knowing anyone in your classes and feeling more isolated can make the experience even more stressful. Additionally, as a brother in MED I would hope to gain valuable volunteering experience in healthcare. Having many connections to outside organizations and non-profits I find to be incredibly valuable, so being granted the opportunity to participate and gain such experience is invaluable. Though I have experience with volunteering, getting healthcare volunteering experience that is more targeted to my long-term professional goals is a large objective of mine. Additionally, being around like-minded peers and driven students will only push me harder to be the best student I can and excel in my classes. Being around those who prioritize their academics is extremely motivating, so being a part of the brotherhood would push me even more to be the best student and mentor I can be.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: In joining MED, what I would hope to contribute to the brotherhood would include my determination, strong work-ethic, creativity, optimism, strong teamwork and independent-work skills, and kindness. Given the opportunity, I believe I could demonstrate to the brothers that I am deeply dedicated to working towards being a healthcare professional, and in doing so, would hope to exemplify my skills as a team player, as well as how I can thrive when given an independent task. I also would love to illustrate my creativity as a future healthcare provider, as it is important to keep patients and peers interested, intrigued, and curious. Additionally, with my experience as a preschool teacher, I have strong skills working with a younger population, so participating in volunteer opportunities working with children is a strong goal of mine, and I would love to support my brothers during such an event if given the chance. Similarly, with such experience, I have exemplified to other peers and employers the empathy, kindness, and optimism that is paramount in such an environment. As a preschool teacher, not only did I play an important role in the children's lives, but also the parents’ lives. Having experience with different populations, being able to work with others in a team and independently, and being hardworking are all crucial to my job, and therefore would be traits I could bring to the Mu Epsilon Delta brotherhood.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: As a preschool teacher, I have had ample experience assisting others and making individuals feel more comfortable in environments that are unfamiliar to them. As I hope to pursue a career as a pediatric physical therapist, having direct experience in the classroom teaching others and finding ways to simplify and orient new or confusing concepts in ways that are easily digestible has become a skill of mine. Moreover, working with an age group so young, finding ways to manage emotions and build trust with those you are working with is crucial to providing the best care you can. It is my belief that this experience translates significantly into the care you are able to provide working in healthcare, regardless of field or specialty. Furthermore, at the University of Tampa I work as a resident assistant. Going into my second year in the role, I have gained substantial knowledge on what it means to care for my peers and how I can support them in their day-to-day lives. It often goes unnoticed what the people around us in college experience and how everyone has their own story, struggles, and successes, so getting to take the time to get to know each of my residents and demonstrate the care I have for all of them will reflect through the work I yield as a healthcare provider in the future. Regarding my experience through volunteering, having the greater portion of my familiarity having been with animal populations additionally demonstrates how much empathy, integrity, and determination goes into caring for truly any population. When volunteering at an animal sanctuary, I underestimated how much effort would go into looking after animals, but I knew that I wanted to continue coming back and caring for those animals because I wanted to see them progress, prosper, and live their best lives. As a future physical therapist, I hope to do the same with my patients and assist them in achieving all of their goals, no matter what.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
Documents like my resume and transcript will tell you all about my academic path in Allied Health and 5 years of competitive rowing. What those documents do not tell you is the moment my feet were set on the path of medicine, the same moment my feet hit the cold hospital floor and I took my first steps on a brand-new hip in July of 2024.

Undergoing a major orthopedic surgery as a student-athlete is jarring. My hip had quietly been failing me for years due to developmental dysplasia. Despite anticipating the procedure for months, it still shook me to suddenly lose my baseline mobility, strength, and independence. 

What grounded me through those scary moments was my Surgical PA. She didn’t just treat me like a chart or something broken to fix. She looked up from my chart and saw a scared, stubborn, and determined 16-year-old who was desperate to feel like herself again and return to her active lifestyle. She educated me on the procedure, listened to my recovery goals, and advocated for details as small as incision placement and aftercare so I could still feel comfortable wearing a swimsuit.

When I stepped onto this campus, I tackled my freshman rowing season and powered through the grueling physical rehabilitation required at the collegiate level. As I settled into college, I deliberately stepped back from competitive athletics to dedicate my full attention to my academics and hands-on clinical experience. Every hour spent studying is driven by the same relentless determination I discovered when learning how to walk a second time. 

That intimate experience is why I am pursuing a career as a surgical Physician Assistant. Healthcare is not just an academic path. It is a personal discipline built on trust, precision, resilience, and relentless patient advocacy.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
Transitioning from a patient facing major joint reconstruction to an undergraduate studying medical sciences can feel isolating. It is hard to find people on campus who share my values and connection to healthcare. What I am hoping to gain from Mu Epsilon Delta is an active and grounded community of individuals like myself who understand that healthcare isn't just a GPA checkbox, it's a calling built on accountability and empathy. 

While my coursework at UTampa and clinical hours at Trinity Wellness Center will give me the technical foundation, I am looking to MED for the individual mentorship and perspective that only a dedicated pre-health network can provide. I want to learn alongside students who understand the demands of clinical practice and hold each other to a higher standard. 

As someone aiming for a career as a surgical Physician Assistant, I am looking to MED for mentorship from upperclassmen who have already navigated difficult courses, clinical hours, and PA school applications. I want to study with peers who are equally as dedicated to bettering themselves for their future patients. 

Beyond academics, I am looking for a fraternity culture that offers mutual support and shared drive, bringing my own experiences with resilience, patient advocacy, and discipline into a community of peers who will continue to push one another.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
My five years of competitive crew taught me that teamwork isn’t about individual success. It is about working toward a communal goal while sitting backward, moving forward in total synchronization, and pulling together when you can’t see the finish line. I bring that same direction and drive to Mu Eplilon Delta.

Having undergone major orthopedic surgery, I know what it means to rebuild from the ground up. That experience forged grit and discipline that dictate how I approach both my medical sciences coursework and my clinical responsibilities at Trinity Wellness Center. That grit means digging in when courses get difficult, or a shift makes you think twice. 

Finally, I bring a deeply empathetic patient-first perspective. I have been on the operating table while working toward one day standing over that very table. Because of that, I know how to listen actively, advocate fiercely, and look beyond the medical chart. 

I am observant, determined, and prepared to be a teammate who pulls her full weight in this chapter. I hope to bring the same resilience, empathy, and willingness to serve to MED while learning from the people around me.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
Balancing the intense physical and mental demands of being a student-athlete throughout all of high school and part of college alongside my education has taught me how to manage high-pressure environments without losing focus. Waking up before dawn for grueling training sessions requires a level of discipline that translates directly to studying and navigating rigorous pre-med requirements. It taught me how to push through physical and mental exhaustion, stay organized when schedules get chaotic, and show up reliably for my team. 

That same sense of accountability and resilience was forged on a much more personal level in July of 2024, when I underwent major joint reconstruction surgery. Spending time on the other side of the surgical drapes as a patient developed my perspective on healthcare. It gave me firsthand insight into the vulnerability of patients and the impact of empathetic care. My own medical experiences have shaped my understanding of what patients endure and the importance of making them feel heard, respected, and supported.

Working as a seasonal administrative assistant and front desk receptionist at Trinity Wellness Center has allowed me to connect those experiences with a clinical environment. Interacting directly with patients, managing scheduling, and observing physical therapists in a clinical setting taught me how vital clear communication and administrative competence are to running a supportive practice. I learned how to read a room, ease patient anxiety, and manage the fast-paced flow of a busy healthcare office. 

Additionally, my experience working as a summer camp counselor at Piedmont Wildlife Center’s Wake location sharpened my leadership, patience, and adaptability. Managing groups of kids and collaborating with fellow staff members required clear communication, quick problem-solving, and emotional intelligence–skills that are essential when working on a multidisciplinary healthcare team.  

Together, these experiences have prepared me to enter healthcare with discipline, resilience, empathy, and a strong sense of responsibility. They have taught me not only how to work hard, but how to remain dependable, communicate effectively, and care for others when they are at their most vulnerable.

Everyone in MED is going through the same things and managing similar pressures that not everyone at Tampa is. That being said, MED is a place that feels safe to me in the sense that I know I'm not alone and everyone is going through it with me! Being a member of MED provides a sense of belonging because I know that I will always have people supporting me!

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: For as long as I can remember, I've been told that I work well with people. I believe the ability to work side by side with whomever is a skill that would benefit MED. I am able to work well with a team towards a shared goal! Another strong skill of mine is my time management. In high school, school was very demanding at times, yet I was still able to be president of two clubs and work as an executive for the NHS. I learned very important time optimization skills during high school that I believe can play a role in my impact at MED. I also consider public speaking one of my best skills. Public speaking is something I was introduced to at a very young age and with time the skill only flourished. I believe that my ability to publicly speak and share my ideas in-front of others is an important attribute to MED. As for traits, my strengths are being compassionate, approachable, and determined. My family and friends always tell me how compassionate I am because I'm able to listen to others well, understand and support others, and build strong relationships. I believe my compassion and approachability work side by side. I have also always been told I am approachable which I believe benefits MED because many different people are a part of this organization and being able to correspond and work alongside others while making them feel comfortable is a strength. Lastly, my determinism is a quality I would like to bring into MED. When I have a goal or dream, I like to see it all the way through. I have many goals and aspirations in pursuing my degree and I believe my determinism towards those ambitions will benefit MED as much as they will benefit me.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: I got my very first job when I was twelve years old in customer service and my most recent job now, at eighteen years old, is still in customer service. Starting at a young age, I adapted good skills in working with others! I believe that my years in customer service only made me more compassionate and understanding of how diverse all humans are which is a vital comprehension of those in healthcare. Some customers would be the sweetest person you've met, then the next the rudest. But yet, you still had to remain yourself. Working in healthcare you must be able to deal with all kinds of various people while still remaining compassionate and collected, which I know my jobs prepared me for! In addition, my jobs aren't just what prepared me for being a healthcare worker, but as well as my volunteer experiences. The two most noteworthy volunteer experiences that I believe prepared me for nursing are being a coach for the Special Olympics and volunteering at the Acts Community Thrift Shop. The Special Olympics  is a program for young children from the ages 2-7 that struggle with Special Needs and Down syndrome that helps them engage in physical activities. I was a coach at my local Special Olympics for two years. Working with the sweet kids was so rewarding but also challenging at times. You had to be prepared when kids went from ecstatic to devastated and angry within seconds, which strengthened my resilience and patience and understanding of the complex nature of humans. My volunteer experience at Acts Community Thrift Shop also taught me a lot. Acts Community Thrift Shop is a local thrift to my community where I have been volunteering for two summers now. The store is incredibly busy and the work is demanding. There were early mornings when I didn't want to get out of bed or days at the store when the work got so intense I fell tired. But, it truly taught me how to not be motivated by internal energy, but internal passion for the impact you're making. It also taught me how to work well with others in high stress times and how to not let the pressure others feel fall onto you because you are your own person! I believe these are all attributes that will help me succeed in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Through joining MED, I hope to find a community of hardworking and like-minded students who encourage one another to strive for academic and personal success. I would love to build meaningful connections with students who share my interest in pursuing a career in healthcare and learn from their experiences and perspectives. I also hope to gain exposure to new volunteer opportunities, extracurricular experiences, and resources that will help me grow both personally and professionally as I prepare for medical school. Most importantly, I hope MED will challenge me to become a more well-rounded student and future healthcare professional while allowing me to contribute to and learn from a supportive community.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I believe my strong work ethic, passion, and communication skills could contribute positively to MED. I tend to stay organized, committed, and dependable with my academics and medical-related things, whilst also including flexibility and initiative when demanded. I am also eager to learn and open to feedback, as I'm always striving to do better for myself and those around me. I believe these qualities would add to the MED whilst also gaining valuable experience.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: I am so happy this question is asked, as I truly believe my curiosity for the medical field began with simple high school hospital volunteering. I volunteered at two hospitals, where I had one-on-one patient care experiences and got to see what working in a hospital was like behind the scenes. I loved it so much that I volunteered every day from freshman year to senior year and even received an award for my commitment. I also started a Letters of Love chapter at my high school, a club that brings together students once a month to make and design cards for pediatric cancer patients that are distributed to hospitals across the USA. Both of these experiences stand out to me when thinking about a career in healthcare. They not only taught me the importance of organization, hard work, and initiative, but also showed me the human side of medicine. I learned that healthcare is not solely about treating an illness; it is about connecting with patients, showing compassion, and helping people feel supported during difficult moments. My experiences also strengthened my communication skills and taught me how important it is to be adaptable when working with different patients and healthcare professionals. These experiences have prepared me to enter healthcare with a strong work ethic, a willingness to learn, and, most importantly, a genuine desire to make a difference in the lives of others.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose nursing as a major and as a profession because as a child I spent a lot of time in hospitals due to an autoimmune disease. When I was five years old I was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes and seeing the work of the nurses who helped me inspired me to pursue a career in the medical field. I believe nurses do such admirable work and the thought of helping others motivates me to follow this career path. Also the aspect of having such caring people help me when I was scared and did not understand what exactly was happening to me led me to further fall in love with nursing. My passion for healthcare is driven by a commitment to meet patients, especially in their most vulnerable moments, and to serve as a reliable source of comfort.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I am interested in joining MED to surround myself with other people who share my dedication for healthcare. notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My volunteer work in the Hackensack Meridian Hospital gave me a first hand look on what my future responsibilities will be as a nurse. It gave me a realistic view on the job and further showed me how much nurses do and their huge impact on the hospital. Even though I wasn't directly working with patients, I was able to help behind the scenes and perform actions that indirectly helped the patients of the hospital. This opportunity gave me insight on the nurses' daily duties and how they truly make an impact on people's lives. I also got to understand the team work and community that came with working in a hospital. As someone that was a part of a dance team throughout high school, I learned many values of team bonding. That experience taught me how to collaborate under pressure, and seeing those same dynamics in a hospital setting reassured me that I am ready for the teamwork and fast-paced demands of nursing. While this isn't direct volunteer work regarding type 1 diabetes, since I was diagnosed I have been participating in various walks, fundraisers, and attending events that raise awareness for this disease. Those experiences are some of the most valuable to me and helped shape my desire for being a nurse.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare

I want to become a healthcare professional who can provide quality care and also advocate for those who face barriers to receiving it. I'm so incredibly lucky that my love for science and my passion for people and service can come together in one place. I hope to use my career to ensure that everyone is cared for regardless of their circumstances.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

I would be looking forward to being a part of a community of like minded people who share my passion for medicine and are committed to pursuing careers centered around serving others. I hope to build meaningful relationships with other pre-health students, learn from their experiences and have the opportunity to both give and receive support through the challenges of pursuing medicine. I also hope MED will help me grow as a person and future physician by providing opportunities to develop leadership, service and professional skills. I hope to grow as a well rounded student and future healthcare professional prepared academically and socially by understanding how important it is to have compassion and teamwork skills.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I believe I would contribute strong dedication, compassion, enthusiasm and genuine willingness to support those around me. I am someone who values teamwork very deeply and I believe that having a positive and supportive attitude in life is one of the key ways of going about this rough pre-health path. I understand the importance of discipline, time management and perseverance, especially when pursuing a challenging academic career. I truly believe I would be a contribution to MED as someone who can bring people together, celebrate their successes and remind them that we are all in this together. I would also bring a strong sense of perseverance and a willingness to step outside of my comfort zone, whether that be taking on leadership, serving my community or helping another member succeed.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences as a medical assistant and phlebotomist, hospital volunteer, middle school ministry leader, and full-time student have each taught me valuable lessons I believe will be essential to a career in healthcare. Working directly with patients as a medical assistant and phlebotomist has taught me to be attentive and professional while helping people feel comfortable during vulnerable moments. Volunteering in a hospital has given me a broader understanding of the healthcare environment and shown me how important teamwork and genuine care is to a patient's experience at the hospital. Leading a middle school children's ministry has strengthened my patience and communication skills and allowed me to grow my ability to connect with people from different backgrounds, while also teaching me to lead with empathy and responsibility. Balancing these commitments with also being a full-time student really challenged me to develop strong time management and discipline skills. These experiences showed me that healthcare was so much more than science and medical school and how it is truly about serving people, communicating effectively, building trust with those around you and being someone who is dependable.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose to major in Public Health because I have always been interested in healthcare and learning about the different things that can affect a person’s health. I like that Public Health focuses not only on individual people, but also on how we can improve the health of entire communities. I think it will give me a different perspective on healthcare that will be helpful in my future career.

My professional track is pre-dental because my goal is to become a dentist. I have always liked working with and helping others, and I became even more interested in dentistry after getting the opportunity to spend time in a dental office and see what the career is actually like. I really like that dentistry combines science with working directly with people and allows you to build relationships with your patients.

What makes me passionate about healthcare is knowing that I can have a positive impact on someone’s life. As a future dentist, I want my patients to feel comfortable, cared for, and confident in their health. I also hope that studying Public Health will help me better understand the barriers that can prevent people from getting the care they need and how I can make a difference in my own community.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I am hoping to gain most from MED is the opportunity to meet other students who are also passionate about healthcare and have similar goals. As a Public Health major on the pre-dental track, I think being surrounded by people pursuing different areas of healthcare would help me learn more about the field as a whole and grow both personally and professionally.

I also hope to gain more experience and knowledge that will help prepare me for my future career. Since my goal is to become a dentist, I would love to learn from other members, hear about their experiences, and get advice from students who are further along in their healthcare journey. I think having a community of people who understand the challenges that come with pursuing a healthcare career would be really valuable.

Most importantly, I hope MED gives me a way to become more involved on campus while doing something that relates to what I am passionate about. I am excited about the opportunity to make new friendships, participate in service opportunities, and be part of a group that encourages and supports each other as we work toward our future careers in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
I think some of the biggest things I would bring to MED are being hardworking, dependable, outgoing, and willing to learn. I really enjoy meeting new people and being involved, so I would want to participate in MED events, service opportunities, and anything else that helps me get more involved in the group.

I also work well with others and like being part of a team. Being involved in sports throughout high school taught me a lot about communication, responsibility, and supporting the people around me. I know how important it is to show up, follow through on what I say I am going to do, and be someone that others can count on.

I would also bring a positive attitude and an open mind. Since MED includes students interested in many different areas of healthcare, I think it is really interesting to be around people who have different goals and experiences. I enjoy learning from other people and hearing different perspectives.

Overall, I think I would be someone who is excited to be involved and contribute wherever I can. I would bring my interest in healthcare and dentistry, while also being supportive of the other members and their goals.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My jobs, volunteering, and extracurricular activities have helped me learn a lot of skills that I think will be important in healthcare. One of the biggest parts of my high school experience was playing volleyball. Being on a team taught me how to communicate with others, manage my time, and stay calm when things get stressful. I was also a team captain, which taught me how to be a leader and support my teammates when they needed me.

Volunteering has also taught me a lot about working with different people. I have had the opportunity to volunteer with people with disabilities, which taught me to be patient, understanding, and open-minded. I learned that everyone communicates differently and that sometimes you have to adjust how you approach a situation to make someone feel comfortable.

I have also spent time in a dental office, which has been one of the experiences that made me realize I really want to become a dentist. I was able to see how the dentist and staff worked together and how they made patients feel comfortable, especially when they were nervous. It showed me that healthcare is not only about knowing the medical side of things, but also about being someone your patients can trust.

All of these experiences have taught me how important communication, teamwork, patience, and responsibility are. I think they have helped prepare me for a future in healthcare and have made me even more excited to continue working toward becoming a dentist.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
My path as a Biology and Pre-Med student is driven by my lifelong goal of becoming a Dermatologist. All of my academic choices, extracurricular commitments, and overall dedication to medicine have all been driven by that singular goal.

My passion for healthcare is deeply rooted in my family, as I have watched my father practice dermatology and witnessed firsthand the impact he has had on his patients' lives. Beyond treating people, I have learned through my experiences how important community is in healthcare, and how, in many areas of medicine, building relationships with those around you is vital. 

Ultimately, my passion is driven by my values of connecting and caring for my community, which I grew up observing.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Through MED, I hope to build lifelong friendships and meaningful connections with brothers who share my passion for healthcare, as well as gain opportunities to volunteer and participate in different specialties of medicine.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: My strong communication skills, open-mindedness, and approachability would help me build meaningful connections and contribute to the inclusive environment in MED. As a natural leader, I like to take initiative and help guide others, while also prioritizing collaboration. I look forward to the opportunity to strengthen the MED community and eventually take on a leadership role to help support members!

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My clinical and leadership experiences have prepared me for the responsibilities of a career in healthcare by exposing me to different environments, allowing me to build a well-rounded mindset and leadership abilities. 

Serving as President of my school’s Pre-Med Program, I had the opportunity to participate in clinical training at FAU Medical School, make rounds at West Boca Medical Center, and hear from healthcare professionals across various specialties, providing me with hands on experiences. I also took part in a four-year internship at the Dermatology Center of Wellington, which taught me essential bedside manner and the basics of Dermatology.

Along with this, I served as President of the Science National Honor Society, Vice President of the National Honor Society, and Vice President of the Math Honor Society, all of which shaped my abilities to organize events, manage logistics, and lead teams. Additionally, founding a skincare blog for teens allowed me to help give back to my community by sharing accessible health information.

All of these have provided me with the experiences  and skills needed to be successful in a healthcare career.

candidates.name: Natasha Webster
facts: Familiar with a current brother: Carla Sales. We worked together in my UTLIT 203 class.
Currently involved in: I am the Secretary of the Caribbean Student Association (CSA).

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
When choosing a major, biology has always felt like the obvious choice for me. I've always known I wanted to be a veterinarian, and growing up on an island surrounded by wildlife made the decision even easier.  
 
I have plenty of stories of how I grew a passion for helping animals, but the one that sticks with me is about a baby falcon. One day, my dad found a skinny baby falcon in our driveway that couldn't fly yet, and there was no mother falcon in sight. For a couple of weeks, we nursed the falcon back to health. I would wake up before elementary school and catch lizards for the falcon. During this time, I felt a deep connection to this bird, and it changed the way I view animals. I started to view them and value them just as much as humans. This may not seem like a big realization, but it was when I was 9 years old.  

I am passionate about healthcare because my community back home in the Virgin Islands lacks healthcare and resources. There are two vet clinics, and they are unprofessional. It's also very hard to get an appointment in a timely manner. In the future, I want to open a vet clinic on my island that provides great service and shows true compassion for animals.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I am hoping to gain a sense of community from MED. Currently, I lack any friends who are also pre-vet, and I think being a part of MED would grant me the opportunity to meet people with similar goals and interests as me. I also find it very frustrating when I am so busy with my work and my friends aren't. Meeting more people with a similar workload would be comforting and motivating. I also want to learn from the upperclassmen in MED and how they are navigating their career goals.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
My strong communication, creativity, and collaboration skills would contribute positively to MED. For all 4 years of high school, I played varsity volleyball, which strengthened my communication and collaboration skills. From this experience, I learned that both of these skills take patience and understanding. During my senior year of high school, I was the Director of the student media team. This experience strengthened my creativity because I created intriguing posters, emails, and social media posts to keep students engaged.   

These experiences taught me how to work well with many different people, communicate clearly, and approach challenges creatively. I would also contribute to MED by listening and learning from my peers, while also contributing my own ideas.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
Over the years, I have gained experience that has better prepared me for a career in healthcare. Firstly, I worked as a church camp counselor for two years, which may not seem like a big job, but it taught me a lot. I learned how to calm people down when they were stressed or upset, which strengthened my patience and problem-solving skills. These skills are useful in healthcare because patients often come in frantic and scared. Secondly, I was the assistant manager of an açaí bowl store back home, where I learned great customer service skills and leadership. These skills are useful because, as a doctor in general, you have to treat your patients kindly, promptly, and confidently.  Lastly, I have volunteered at my local humane society multiple times, which has taught me basic animal care. 

I still have a lot of room to grow as I prepare to become a veterinarian. I also need guidance, and I think MED would be the perfect place for me to start.

I was especially interested in the gift of life volunteering opportunity through MED fraternity, and I would be grateful to get involved and contribute to making a positive impact in the movement. This is one example of the impact I want to make as a member of MED, and I would like to get involved in a variety of similar opportunities that uplift various groups and communities.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: Upon joining MED, I believe my dedication, timeliness, and organization will greatly contribute to the fraternity. I spent the majority of my time shadowing observing patient interactions, each with a different set of circumstances, which was an eye-opening experience that showed me the gentle care, professionalism, and knowledge that is required to provide patients with the utmost level of care. When I was not observing patient interactions, I spent my time talking to and gaining insight from faculty members including APRN's, Physicians, and other PA's. Also, I took notes on every new piece of information and terminology that I encountered so that I could begin building the foundation that will support me as I progress through both the academic and clinical process of the pre-PA track. In addition to this experience, I have been a retail sales associate at various running specialty stores for over four years. This job mostly includes providing customers with the proper running shoes by walking them though a detailed fitting process that includes both a static and dynamic gait analysis. I look at pressure scans, foot measurements, weight bearing, and movement patterns to fit a customer into the proper shoe so that they can continue along their running and fitness journey successfully. I find it extremely important to explain to each customer my observations as well as the footwear selections I made based on their foot scan and gait analysis. As a result, customers can walk away feeling confident in their decision and motivated to continue running. I feel both of these experiences have and will continue to prepare me for taking on greater responsibilities in a healthcare setting because I am improving my ability to interact with patients, beginning to develop my practical skills in a healthcare setting, and setting the highest possible standard for the level of care that I will strive to provide patients with when I have the responsibilities that come with a career in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
During the COVID-19 quarantine, social media was one of the few ways I could stay connected to the outside world. One day, a video appeared on my TikTok of a wildlife conservationist caring for an injured bird and eventually releasing it back into the wild after it had fully recovered. Before seeing that video, I had never known what I wanted to do with my future because I had never felt truly connected to a career. Something about seeing an animal being cared for and then returned to its natural environment immediately sparked an interest in me.
       Because of the algorithm, I soon began seeing more videos about wildlife conservation, rehabilitation, and helping animals. This interest eventually led me to volunteer at North Shore Animal League of America in New York once I was old enough. This was my first real experience with animal care, and it only made me more passionate about the field. I could leave covered in animal waste with stains on my shirt and still be excited to come back the next day. I did not mind the less glamorous parts of the work because I knew I was helping create a better environment for the animals in my care. It was through this experience that I realized I wanted to pursue veterinary medicine, with the hope of eventually working with wildlife.
       I chose Biology as my major because I have always been more drawn to science and math than subjects like English or history. More importantly, biology gives me the scientific foundation I need to understand animals, their health, and the medical care they require. My experiences have shown me that healthcare is not always easy or glamorous, but helping an animal recover and improve its quality of life makes the challenges worthwhile.

Healthcare is a challenging and demanding field, and I believe having people around me who understand those challenges would provide both motivation and support. I hope to form genuine friendships and connections that extend beyond academics and become a meaningful part of my college experience.

Most importantly, I hope to contribute to MED just as much as I gain from it and become an active member of a community that I can truly feel a part of.
