notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My first exposure to animal care was through volunteering at North Shore Animal League of America, a nonprofit animal shelter in New York. There, I learned the basics of caring for dogs and cats while also seeing the struggles and hardships that many animals face. This experience motivated me to become more involved in animal care and ultimately pursue a career where I could help animals in need.
       Over the summer, I gained my first exposure to the medical side of animal care by shadowing at Royal Vet Clinic in Miami. I was able to see what happens behind the scenes of a veterinary practice, including observing procedures such as dental surgeries and neutering. I also learned how to safely handle animals of different sizes when administering medications and gained a better understanding of commonly prescribed medications and their uses. Most importantly, I had the opportunity to speak with veterinarians and veterinary technicians about their experiences and what it is truly like to work in the field. Although I saw how challenging and unpredictable the profession can be, seeing how passionate they were about helping animals showed me that the difficult moments are worth pushing through when you are passionate about your work.
       Outside of veterinary medicine, my customer service jobs at a bakery and an acai shop have also prepared me for a career in healthcare. These experiences taught me the importance of hard work, determination, communication, and patience. Working directly with customers pushed me out of my comfort zone and helped me become more confident in speaking with and assisting others. I believe these skills will be especially valuable in healthcare, where communication, teamwork, and the ability to remain patient and professional are essential. Together, my experiences have taught me how to work with others, handle responsibility, and remain committed to helping others, which are qualities I hope to carry into my future career in healthcare.

As much as I want to learn from this experience, I also want to be a source of encouragement and support for students like me throughout the Pre-PA journey. While pursuing a profession in healthcare is demanding and stressful, it is important to be optimistic and an approachable person whom those around you enjoy being around.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My jobs as a Patient Care Technician and lab mentor, as well as taking part in extracurricular activities such as the University of Tampa’s Pre-PA Club, Women in Medicine Club, Medi-Futures Program, and VAW Global Health Alliance, have been crucial to preparing me for a career in health care. Firstly, as a lab mentor for general chemistry, I have developed my leadership and communication skills as I am a mentor to many students. Through this role, I am able to help students better understand material and serve as a source of guidance. Working with both the instructor and students, the patience and skills I have acquired will be crucial as a healthcare provider when communicating with patients and having to work alongside other providers. In addition, my experience as a PCT on the mother baby/postpartum unit at the hospital back home has given me direct exposure to patient care. Through this, I have acquired clinical skills such as taking vitals signs, phlebotomy, EKG’s, foley care, and circumcisions. While these are important skills to learn, it has taught me that healthcare is much more than performing these skills; compassion, responsibility, and, most importantly, making sure your patients feel understood and respected are important. Moving forward, being a part of the on-campus clubs has allowed me to further explore my interests and find exactly what I am interested in pursuing: PA. These organizations have allowed me to connect with other students and have continued to encourage me to pursue a career in healthcare. In addition to these clubs, I completed the Medi-Futures online program this past spring semester, where I gained 40 virtual shadowing hours. Through these hours, I listened to various presentations from many health-care professionals in different fields where we learned about what their job entailed, tasks they performed, and sample patient care cases. Finally, VAW Global Health Alliances is a Medical Outreach program I am traveling to Peru this upcoming January with to medically serve. Throughout this semester, we will attend team training sessions/workshops needed prior to arriving in Peru. Through this experience, we will work alongside the local healthcare professionals to help treat individuals at the medical clinic. Ultimately, I am excited to step out of my comfort zone to learn about how healthcare is different across the world depending on the circumstances, helping develop my cultural awareness and overall skills in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I actually didn't start college on a pre-health track. My first year in Tampa, I was a Marketing major with a minor in PR/Advertising because I thought that was what I wanted to do with my life. It was also the path everyone always told me made sense for me. But I realized it didn't excite me or feel like something I was truly passionate about. Deep down, I have always had a passion for healthcare. Ever since I was little, I wanted to be a pediatrician, but as I got older, other people, and eventually I convinced myself that I didn't have the grades or what it took to pursue medicine. So that dream faded, and I stuck with what everyone told me I was good at. That all changed two summers ago when I decided to shadow my pediatrician and fell in love with healthcare all over again. Being able to take care of patients and create a connection with them reminded me of the dream I had pushed aside for years. It made me realize I would rather work hard for something I truly wanted than choose a path because it felt safer. When I came back for my sophomore year, I changed my major and committed myself to medicine. Not everyone believed in me when I made that decision, but that has only pushed me to work harder and show myself what I'm capable of. Although pediatrics was what originally brought me back to medicine, I became drawn to dermatology because of my grandmother. She was one of the few dermatologists in Puerto Rico at that time, but after becoming ill at a young age, she left that dream behind. Pursuing dermatology now feels incredibly personal to me, so what was once her dream has now become my own.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: In my two years at UT, I honestly haven't felt a sense of community that I always hear people talk about when they describe college. I've joined clubs and gotten involved in different things, but none of them have felt fulfilling to me. I even considered rushing a sorority because I wanted to see what everyone was raving about, but I eventually realized it didn't align with who I am and what I want to achieve. So this year I decided to put myself out there and go out and do new things, even things that are out of my comfort zone. What I hope to gain from MED, beyond experience and knowledge, is finally finding a community of people who share similar goals, interests, and motivation. I want to be surrounded by people who understand how challenging the pre-health path can be, but who can also support each other through it and make the experience less individual. I also want to push myself socially. Since coming to UT, I feel like I've closed myself off to meeting people outside of my immediate friend group, and I want to change that. More than anything, I hope MED becomes a place where I can be challenged, supported, and genuinely connected, while also helping me grow into the person and future healthcare professional I want to become.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I think one of the biggest things I would bring to MED is that I genuinely love to lead and be involved. I'm not really someone who likes to sit back and just watch things happen. I like taking initiative, bringing people together, and making sure things get done. I also love planning things, whether it's a party, lunch, going out with friends, chill movie nights, or something more organized. I take a lot of pride in the things I do, and I like making them as good as possible, not only for my own satisfaction but because I want the people around me to enjoy the result too. I'm also very determined and don't back down easily. I tend to believe there is a solution to almost every problem, so if something doesn't work the first time, I'd rather find another way than to give up. I think that mindset would help me contribute to MED because I'm willing to step up, problem-solve, and take responsibility when needed. I also really enjoy giving back to others and making people feel included, supported, and comfortable. More than anything, I would want to be an active member who brings energy, ideas, and effort into the organization and give back just as much as I hope to gain from it.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
I think my experiences have prepared me for healthcare mostly by showing me that taking care of people looks different depending on who is in front of you. Before I had any real exposure to healthcare, I pictured medicine mostly as diagnosing someone and knowing how to treat them. The more experience I've gained, the more I've realized how much of it is actually about people. Working as a tutor, babysitter, and camp counselor taught me this before I even knew I wanted to pursue medicine. I worked with kids who all had different personalities and needs, and I quickly learned that the same approach does not work for everyone. Sometimes you have to be patient, change how you communicate, or simply make someone feel comfortable enough to trust you. Shadowing made that even more real for me. Pediatrics was the experience that brought me back to healthcare, but since then I have also had exposure to oncology and dermatology. At PanOncology and the Cancer Hospital in Puerto Rico, I shadowed physicians, worked alongside nurses, observed patient care, and learned about ongoing cancer research. Seeing patients go through some of the hardest moments of their lives made me understand that being good at medicine is not enough. Patients are trusting you when they are scared, vulnerable, or unsure of what comes next.
My experiences have also made me realize how important it is to be social and approachable in healthcare. I once had a doctor who was not very engaging, and although that doesn't make them a bad doctor, I remember not feeling fully comfortable opening up about what I needed. That stayed with me because it showed me how much confidence and communication really matter. If patients don't feel safe talking to you, they may hold back in their care. Volunteering has opened my eyes to this too, especially through fostering animals. It made me realize that patience, trust, responsibility, and care don't only apply to people. Whether it's a patient, a child, or an animal depending on you, there is something meaningful about being someone they can feel safe with. These experiences have shown me the kind of healthcare professional I want to become: knowledgeable and capable, but also approachable, confident, and someone others feel comfortable trusting.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare

I’ll never forget watching young kids push IV stands up and down the hallways. Seeing children go through things so much more difficult than I was crushed me. Ever since my experience, the idea of being able to bring light into kids lives while also improving their health means everything. I want to be the doctor that takes time with his patients instead of herding them through the hospital. I have fallen in love with serving people in need of help. I find more fulfillment in that than I ever have doing anything else. I am also a christian and believe that this is the path God has for me. I don’t think many other careers could bring me the level of fulfillment the medical field will.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: The jobs and experiences I have had have taught me skills I believe will be very beneficial to my future career in healthcare. One of my biggest learning experiences was running my own car detailing company in high school. I learned how to communicate with customers, problem solve, and work alongside my co-founder. It was the first thing in my life I had complete and total responsibility for. It taught me how to take ownership of my action and that the world wasn’t as black and white as school made it seem. In school failing a test could mean the end of someones grade and is very looked down upon. However, when I ran my own buisness, most of my learning came through trial and error. It gave me a healthy relationship with failure and showed me that the world doesn’t end when I fail. I know medicine requires extremely high standards but I also know that being a great student and future physician requires constantly learning, accepting feedback, and growing from setbacks. Another oppurtunity I had was to shadow Dr. Nuckols (Ear, Nose Throat surgeon) for a week. I was able to observe Dr. Nuckols interact with patients and also perform surgeries. This experience inside the operating room helped me center my goals on surgery. I was able to watch Nuckols and his team work together in an organized fashion. It taught me so much about teamwork. Everyone in the operating room had a job and relied on eachother to complete them. This showed me just how much you have to trust and maintain healthy relationship with you co-workers. The way Nuckols spoke to his patients pre and post operation also stuck out to me. He sympathized with there worries and made there questions feel heard while also bring a strong sense of confidence. He was able to walk them through there worries and the procedures in a way that made them feel safe. He showed me how important it is to display peaceful body language and manner. I know the responsibilities I will face in healthcare will be much greater, but I believe these experiences have given me a strong foundation to continue building on.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose my major and professional track because my experiences throughout high school showed me that I find the most purpose in helping others, especially during some of their most vulnerable moments. My passion for healthcare developed through volunteering at a hospital, working as a lifeguard and instructor and becoming CPR/First Aid certified. At the hospital, I spent over 200 hours supporting patients and staff in emergency and operations settings. Being around patients and seeing the work that happens behind the scenes gave me a better understanding of the responsibility that comes with caring for someone.
Outside of the hospital, I became deeply involved in community service. I completed over 300 service hours and served as president of my school's Service Club, where I helped organize bimonthly Red Cross blood drives that averaged more than 50 red blood cell donations per event. I also competed in the state SkillsUSA CPR and First Aid competition, placing eighth overall. One experience I am especially proud of was working with a friend to establish three district-wide food pantries throughout our county. Seeing these pantries continue to be restocked and used by people in our community showed me that making an impact goes beyond treating someone when they are sick. It means recognizing when people need help and taking the initiative to do something about it. These experiences have shown me that healthcare is where I can turn my passion for helping others into a meaningful career. I want to work in a field where I can make a difference in someone's life and continue learning how I can better serve the people around me.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Through MED, I hope to gain experiences and guidance that will help me become more prepared for a career in medicine. While my hospital volunteering and other healthcare experiences have given me an introduction to the field, I want to gain more direct clinical exposure and better understand what it is like to pursue medicine as a student. Having people who can share their advice about classes, studying and preparing for a career in medicine would help me make more informed decisions and avoid feeling like I have to figure everything out on my own. I also hope to take advantage of MED's study sessions and academic assistance. I know that pursuing medicine will require me to develop strong study habits and learn how to manage a demanding workload. Being part of a community where I can learn alongside other students would give me the support and motivation to keep improving. Most importantly, I hope MED will help me grow into someone who is more confident and prepared to pursue medicine. I want to gain clinical experience, learn from students who have already been through the process and build relationships with people who share my interest in healthcare. I see MED as an opportunity to learn from others while also contributing my own experiences and commitment to service.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I believe I would contribute to MED through my leadership experience and my willingness to step up when something needs to be done. Serving as president of my Service Club and National Honor Society taught me how to take responsibility for a group and make sure that plans actually turn into action. My experiences have also taught me how to stay calm when situations become stressful. As a lifeguard and instructor, I performed more than 15 aquatic rescues and learned that panicking does not help the person who needs you. I had to assess what was happening and respond quickly. My hospital experience gave me a similar understanding of how important it is to remain focused when working around patients. I also believe that I bring a genuine desire to help others. I have spent more than 300 hours volunteering because service is something I have continued to choose even when I was not required to do it. Helping establish three food pantries with a friend showed me that if I see a problem in my community, I want to find a way to help address it. I know that I still have a lot to learn, and I am comfortable with that. I am willing to ask questions, listen to others and learn from my mistakes. I would bring that mindset into MED while supporting the people around me and making the most of every opportunity.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My jobs, volunteer experiences and extracurricular activities have helped me understand the responsibility that comes with working in healthcare. My hospital volunteering was especially meaningful because I spent over 200 hours working in the emergency and operations center of a hospital that saw more than 100 patients each day. I helped support staff in pre-op and post-op areas, transported patients and restocked supplies. Being in the hospital allowed me to see how many different people contribute to a patient's care and how important it is for everyone to communicate and work together. My time as a lifeguard and instructor also taught me how to interact with people in situations where they may be scared or need reassurance. I learned that helping someone is not always about knowing exactly what to say or do. Sometimes it is about being present, listening and making sure the person feels supported. I believe this is something that will be important when working with patients. My involvement in community service has also helped prepare me for a career centered around serving others. Through more than 300 service hours and my role as Service Club president, I had opportunities to organize events and bring people together around causes that directly benefited our community. Helping establish three district-wide food pantries with a friend also taught me to recognize a need and take action rather than waiting for someone else to address it. Overall, these experiences have shown me that healthcare is a field where I will constantly have opportunities to learn and help others. notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
Ever since I can remember, I have had a strong awareness of what it feels like to be excluded. Moving to a new country at a young age and not being able to fully express myself because I did not know the language made that feeling even stronger. My experiences made me curious about why people feel, think, and behave the way they do, which is a major reason I chose psychology.

I am fascinated by the human mind and the many factors that shape our behavior, from trauma responses and attachment patterns to the experiences that influence the decisions we make. Psychology gives me the opportunity to understand these things while also learning how to support people through some of the most difficult moments of their lives.

I chose to pursue healthcare because I believe healthcare should be for everyone. A person's background, where they come from, or what they believe should never determine the quality of care they receive. I want to be part of a field that treats people with the same level of respect and compassion while recognizing that every patient has their own experiences and needs. I have always found purpose in caring for others and consider myself an attentive and dependable person who genuinely wants people to feel heard and supported.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED

Most importantly, I want MED to be a place where I feel like I belong. Coming from an experience where I have sometimes felt excluded, having a community of people by my side who are working toward similar goals is especially meaningful to me. I hope to leave MED with not only a better understanding of the healthcare path, but also lasting friendships, confidence, and a community that I can rely on throughout my journey.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: From MED, I am hoping to gain meaningful connections through networking with other students in healthcare majors, and a stronger sense of community. As a nursing student, and medical major in general, it is easy for the workload to catch up, so I want to surround myself with people who share my same passion for healthcare and create an understanding of what we are all going through. I am also interested in learning from students with different interests and career goals within the medical field. I hope MED will give me opportunities to grow professionally through mentorship, service, networking, and exposure to the many different areas of healthcare. I also want to become more confident in my leadership and other skills that I can carry with me throughout nursing school and my future career. Last but definitely not least, I hope to gain meaningful friendships with people who motivate and support one another. I want to make friends that share the same values as me, and hopefully gain life-long friends that will continue after college. I want to be an active member of MED who not only learns from the fraternity, but also contribute my own ideas to make this chapter and future chapters memorable. I want the students in the medical route to have a bigger space to introduce their ideas and make a huge impact within the university. I believe being part of MED would challenge me to grow both personally and academically while allowing me to be a part of a community that I can take pride in.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I believe I would contribute a positive attitude, genuine curiosity, and a strong willingness to learn to MED. I am someone who enjoys meeting new people, hearing different perspectives and backgrounds, and putting myself in environments where I can grow. I am also dependable and committed to the load I take on, and I am not afraid to step outside my comfort zone or act on an opportunity I can take and pursue. As someone beginning my nursing journey, I want to learn from those around me and become more knowledgeable about the many different paths within healthcare. I value being approachable and supportive, and I want the people around me to feel comfortable being themselves and sharing their ideas with me. I also bring enthusiasm and energy to the groups I am a part of and enjoy helping create a community where people feel included. I hope to contribute to MED by being an engaged member who participates, supports others, and makes the most of every opportunity the organization provides. I have genuine interest in connecting with others who are part of the pre-med route, and make a positive impact personally and professionally through the MED community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My experiences in leadership, academics, athletics, and employment have helped me develop qualities that I believe are essential to a career in healthcare. While working as a server at Chili's Bar and Grill, I interacted with a variety of customers and learned how important communication, patience, and attention to detail are in an environment that is constantly changing and challenging me. I was responsible for taking orders accurately, keeping track of multiple tables and requests at once, handling payments (cash and card), and working closely with other servers and kitchen staff. This experience taught me how to stay organized and level-headed under pressure, and quickly adapt when situations changed. These skills would carry on to working with patients and collaborating with healthcare professionals. As a Varsity Volleyball Captain, I learned how to communicate effectively, motivate others, and remain supportive during stressful competitions and practices. Being responsible for a team taught me how to recognize different areas of strengths and weaknesses, and how to address those through example and speech. As President of the National Honor Society, I gained experience leading others, organizing fundraising and volunteering events, and facilitating a space where being scholars were valued greatly. As an AVID Tutor, I developed patience and learned how to explain information in different ways while creating an environment where students feel comfortable asking for help. The extracurriculars that I have been involved in have prepared me to enter healthcare with strong communication, teamwork, leadership, patience, and problem-solving skills. I am super excited to continue developing these qualities throughout nursing school and being involved in this MED chapter.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose biology and the pre-dental track because dentistry has been a part of my life for as long as I can remember. I chose biology because I want a strong foundation in the sciences. My mom is a dentist, so I grew up seeing what her work looked like and hearing about her experiences with patients. That early exposure made me interested in dentistry, but as I got older, I wanted to understand for myself what made the field a good fit for me.
What drew me to dentistry is how it incorporates science, hands-on work, and patient interaction. Through shadowing at Park Saratoga Dental with Dr. Kathleen Ban, I have been able to see this firsthand while observing procedures such as fillings, extractions, crowns, and cleanings. I especially enjoy seeing how dentists combine their hands-on skills with how they interact with patients. 
My interest in healthcare has also grown through public health and research. Research helps us understand why health problems happen while public health looks at how we can prevent those problems and reach people before they need treatment. I like looking at health from that bigger perspective and asking why certain communities experience different health outcomes. My experiences have made me realize that I want my future in healthcare to include both treating individual patients and understanding the larger factors that affect their health.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
I am hoping to meet people who are also figuring out what they want their future in healthcare to look like. Starting college and pursuing a healthcare career feels like a lot to navigate, and I think having people around me who understand that experience would make a big difference.
I also want to learn about healthcare outside of just dentistry. Most of my experiences so far have been centered around dental care and public health, so I would like to hear about other fields from people actually pursuing them. I think being around students interested in other health professions would give me perspectives that I would not get from my own experiences.
I am also looking forward to the opportunities MED provides to get involved. I have always enjoyed being part of projects where I can actually contribute, whether that means helping develop an oral health curriculum for children in Uganda or volunteering. I would like to continue doing that in college while getting to know the people I am working with.
Lastly, but most importantly, I want to make friends and create lifelong bonds with others also in the field of healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
One of the biggest things I would contribute to MED is my ability to take initiative. I have often put myself in situations where I had to figure out how to contribute rather than simply follow instructions. For example, while working with the University of Kentucky’s Collaborative Research on Medication Use & Family Health Lab, after being on the Youth Advisory Board and having a team engineer as a guest speaker, I took initiative to meet with them and helped co-design MedSMA℞T, a mobile game focused on opioid misuse. I enjoyed being able to take an idea and help turn it into something that could actually be used.
I would also contribute strong communication skills. As an Indian classical music mentor, I have worked one-on-one with students ranging from ages of 5 to 60, creating lesson plans based on their individual needs. That experience taught me that explaining something well does not mean explaining it the same way to everyone. I have used that same skill in healthcare settings, including when I provided oral hygiene tips to patients while shadowing at Park Saratoga Dental, considering factors such as age and comfortability. 
Another strength I bring is collaboration. While working on my YPAR project with Breathe California, I worked with health specialists to refine a survey about cannabis perceptions among people ages 13–25. I had to be open to feedback while also thinking critically about wording, bias, and how questions could affect the quality of our results. 
Finally, I am comfortable taking on responsibility. As a National Youth Advisory Board Chair for CATCH, I helped oversee the Students-Teach-Students model and led focus groups to assess student educators’ progress. I would bring that same willingness to take responsibility to MED.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences have prepared me for healthcare by teaching me that being a healthcare professional requires much more than knowing science
During my dental shadowing and internship at Park Saratoga Dental, I observed a variety of procedures while paying attention to how providers communicated with patients. I also provided oral hygiene tips to more than 40 patients. Seeing how dentists adjusted their communication based on each patient showed me that clinical knowledge is only effective when a patient understands and trusts their provider.
I am most passionate about my extracurriculars relating to public health, because I like looking at healthcare from a perspective that goes beyond treating someone. That is what initially drew me to advocacy. Through CATCH Global Health Foundation, I worked on vaping prevention education and advocated for youth perspectives to be included in health education. I saw how much the way information is presented can influence whether people actually understand and connect with it. My research experiences have made me interested in a different side of public health as well. At Rose Academies, I have helped develop an oral health curriculum for children in Kampala, Uganda. Experiences like these have shown me that improving healthcare goes beyond what happens between a patient and provider. 
Across these experiences, I have learned to listen before acting and take responsibility for my role on a team. These are skills I hope to continue developing throughout college and eventually bring into my career in healthcare.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose Allied Health on the pre-med track because I have always been interested in how the human body works, but even more importantly, I care about how healthcare makes people feel. Through my own experiences as a patient, I have seen how meaningful it is when a provider listens carefully, takes concerns seriously, and looks beyond the most obvious explanation. Those experiences made healthcare feel personal to me and helped me realize that I want to become the kind of physician who makes patients feel understood rather than overlooked.

Allied Health gives me the opportunity to study health from multiple perspectives instead of focusing only on disease. I am especially interested in prevention, lifestyle, and the way factors such as nutrition, movement, stress, and environment can affect a person’s overall health. At the same time, the pre-med track will provide the strong scientific foundation I need to understand complex medical conditions and eventually care for patients responsibly.

I am passionate about healthcare because it combines science with human connection. Medicine requires knowledge and careful decision-making, but it also requires empathy, trust, and the ability to meet people during some of their most vulnerable moments. I want a career where I can continue learning while making a direct difference in people’s lives. Ultimately, I hope to practice medicine in a way that treats the whole person, encourages patients to take an active role in their health, and helps them feel genuinely supported throughout their care.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I hope to gain most from MED is a strong community of students who can support each other in this field of study. As a freshman, I would love to surround myself with motivated people who share similar goals while bringing different perspectives and interests to the organization. I hope MED becomes a place where I can form genuine friendships, ask questions, and feel supported throughout my pre-pa journey.

I am also excited about the opportunity to build meaningful professional relationships. Connecting with older students, and healthcare professionals would allow me to learn from their experiences and better understand the many paths available within medicine. I hope to gain mentors who can offer honest guidance while also developing relationships with peers whom I may one day work alongside in the healthcare field.

Finally, I want to take advantage of the service, leadership, shadowing, and professional development opportunities MED provides. Classroom learning is important, but I believe experiences outside the classroom are what help students grow into compassionate and capable healthcare professionals. Through MED, I hope to explore my interests, strengthen my confidence, and become more prepared for medical school and my future career. I also want to contribute to the organization by supporting other members and helping build the same sense of community that I hope to find.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
The traits I would contribute to MED are engagement, dependability, initiative, and a genuine desire to connect with others and create a community. I care deeply about making people feel included, especially in environments that can feel unfamiliar or intimidating. I believe this would help me support other members and contribute to a welcoming community.

I am also responsible and committed. Organizing Race for Your Heart during all four years of high school taught me how to take initiative, manage responsibilities, and consistently follow through. My two years working at iCRYO strengthened my communication skills and taught me how to remain professional while interacting with people who have different personalities, needs, and health goals.

Another trait I would bring to MED is curiosity. I enjoy learning about healthcare beyond the classroom and exploring alternative methods found in new research. I am open-minded, willing to ask questions, and excited to learn from both my peers and professionals.

Most importantly, I would be an active member rather than someone who simply attends meetings. I would participate in service opportunities, support other members, and contribute ideas when possible. I hope to bring a positive and thoughtful presence to MED while helping create the kind of community where students encourage one another and grow together.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences working at iCRYO for two years and organizing the American Heart Association’s Race for Your Heart throughout all four years of high school have prepared me for healthcare in different but equally important ways.

At iCRYO, I worked in a health and wellness environment where I regularly interacted with people who had different goals, concerns, and comfort levels. That experience taught me how important it is to listen closely, communicate clearly, and help each person feel comfortable and cared for. I also learned that trust is built through small actions, such as being dependable, remaining patient, and treating every person with respect. Working there strengthened my professionalism and showed me that health is not one-size-fits-all. Each person brings a different background and reason for seeking support, which is something I will carry with me into a future career in medicine.

Organizing Race for Your Heart for four consecutive years allowed me to contribute to healthcare from a community perspective. Because the race supported the American Heart Association, I was able to help raise awareness about heart health while bringing people together around an important cause. Planning the event required leadership, organization, communication, and the ability to follow through on long-term responsibilities. Continuing it each year also taught me that meaningful service requires consistency, not just a single act.

Together, these experiences have helped me become a stronger communicator, leader, and team member. They taught me to take responsibility for others, remain attentive to individual needs, and approach health with both compassion and initiative. Most importantly, they confirmed that I want a career centered on serving people and helping them live healthier lives.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
I chose to become an Allied Health major with a Physician Assistant track because, from a logical standpoint, it will help guide me in the best route to becoming a dermatologist. The first time I heard about Allied Health as a major, that was one of the biggest reasons why I fell in love with The University of Tampa. The classes I have and will be taking were extremely fascinating to me, and I knew that these courses, along with this major, would be the right path for me to gain the most knowledge so that I can become the best health care provider I can be.
I am extremely passionate about health care because one of the things I strive to do in life is influence people’s lives for the greater good. A medical setting can be extremely nerve-wracking for a lot of patients; I want to be a health care provider that a patient never forgets by making them as comfortable and cared for as possible. Though my top goal is to become a PA in dermatology, I find all aspects of health care incredibly intriguing. I aim to gain as much experience and knowledge as I can. This will guarantee my confidence in where I stand in regards to my goals and position in health care.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: After attending the information sessions, I learned a lot more about Mu Epsilon Delta than I already knew. Right off the bat, I could tell the connections are so strong in this community. I haven’t had great opportunities to connect with people in the same or similar majors as me. I believe that MED will give me a much greater chance to make some new friends and memories with people who are like-minded. I am also very excited about earning clinical hours as well as more volunteering opportunities. Clinical hours is something that everyone needs, I’m looking forward to the exposure of medical experiences that comes with it. I have also really enjoyed volunteering for things in the past, so it will be amazing to get more chances to make a difference in the community. There will also be study sessions for anything that needs to be studied like classes or official state tests to get into the program necessary after undergrad. This will be extremely helpful for me as I will be able to learn strategies from other brothers that have and are going through the same thing as I am.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
I have great teamwork and communication skills. If I’m in a group and everyone's nervous to speak up or take the lead, I step up to help push everyone to get comfortable with themselves and what their role might be, while making sure that everyone’s voice and opinions have been heard. I am a very empathetic person and a great listener. I am always willing to listen to someone when there’s an issue going on; if they don’t want to talk about it, I will distract them, sit in silence with them, absolutely anything they need, I will be there. I have integrity; I couldn’t lie even if I wanted to. I also want to gain the trust of my peers and future patients. Sometimes the truth can be hard to hear and even share. Nonetheless, if the truth is necessary, you owe that person honesty.
I also have experience with medical equipment. For example, I’ve learned how to suture, properly use a microscope, casting, prepping medicine or formula, and conduct research throughout high school, as well as my time in undergrad.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: All of my volunteer experiences have helped me believe in myself and gain confidence in my leadership skills. Using my creative thinking in regards to choreography for shows and performances, I proved to myself that I am a good leader by reassuring the people present, making sure they’re following along, and making sure they receive the help they need. It also showed me the actual directors’ point of view and how stressful and difficult it is for them, which leads me to my empathy for people. Volunteering at an animal rescue for over five and a half years has made me appreciate animals so much more. It also taught me how to handle working with other coworkers that seem a little difficult, or like to do things differently than others. Mainly, it taught me how to care, as well as be alert of things or people and animals. Seeing that there were baby animals (I.e goats, pigs, birds), I had to learn how to make baby formula, and become a nurturing figure for those animals that didn’t have a parent. I was also always on the lookout for any abnormalities that might be concerning for an animal. Whenever I did spot something, I reported it to the shift leader(s) as soon as I could. It taught me responsibility; I made sure everything was taken care of for the animals, making sure they had food, water, a clean stall, and lots of TLC. Volunteering at an animal rescue showed me that no matter what condition you are in physically or mentally (this was up north, so when winter came, the weather was brutally cold), the job still had to get done. I didn’t care about how cold I was. I cared more about whether or not the animals were taken care of and stayed as warm as possible. This also exposed me to loss and death. Some of my favorite animals were either adopted or, unfortunately, couldn’t be saved from their condition. It was really hard because of the strong connections I had made with them. However if it meant them going to a loving family, or crossing the rainbow bridge to be relieved of the pain, I knew it was the best thing to do for them. For that, I will always be grateful for the lessons and skills I have gained from volunteering at an animal rescue.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: In high school I always went back and forth between different career paths and majors but they all always had one thing in common, a desire to serve my community. I went from social work, to prosecution, and even considered education. Then I stumbled upon healthcare and I knew it was what I wanted to do right away. It not only combines that desire for helping the community but it also carries the importance of life. Without health there is no way to function, and I wanted to be at the forefront of that. I chose Biology as my major and pre-med for my pre-professional track because it allowed me to not only get the knowledge I need for medical school but it also gives me the background for understanding the connection between the human body on a biological or cellular level and patient care. My passion for healthcare stems from the science of being able to understand the physical body. These are some of the reasons why I want to go into surgery specifically, paired with the connection between the patient and the provider. When people are not in good health they are scared and vulnerable. Having someone be able to place their complete trust in you especially in the operating room is what ignited my passion for pre-med in the first place.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: I hope to gain a driven community in which I can feel comfortable, be challenged, and find support that helps me propel forward and vice versa. Since the pre-health track is so vigorous sometimes it can feel isolating but having Mu Epsilon Delta would give me people who have similar goals and passion, who understand the academic rigor and who can push each other to succeed. Through community I also hope  to make connections in healthcare that are meaningful. Communicating with upperclassmen who have been in my position and understand my path will give me very valuable insight on how applications work, career opportunities and research. I view my gain as a mutual benefit in which I get to absorb the knowledge and encouragement of my peers while also giving them my own perspective and background, being someone they can depend on and feel encouraged by. As I continue forward I hope to get the honor of passing down the mentorship to new members, ensuring they feel the same community that I hope to gain and that Mu Epsilon Delta is an uplifting environment for all members on the pre-health track.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I will contribute to Mu Epsilon Delta by being an approachable study partner, an observant team member, and a dedicated contributor to service events. My mindset when it comes to teamwork is very collaborative. In an academic or professional space my goal is to create an environment where no one feels hesitant to ask questions. I really enjoy being able to break down material in a way that is easier for everyone to understand, and friends often reach out to me to work through issues. I want to bring that patience into chapter study sessions by asking questions and collaborating openly. In these group settings I tend to be an observant team player who listens and evaluates all the perspectives of a group. Even though I am a bit more reserved myself, I am always willing to step forward when direction is needed. I look forward to bringing this work ethic into philanthropic events where I hope to be working hard and showing up to be a supportive part of the chapter’s community, being a dependable hand when needed.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: Throughout high school and into college, my extracurriculars and jobs have given me a very realistic understanding of the responsibility that comes with healthcare. It isn't just about learning biology or doing well on exams; it’s about learning how to be accountable, stay calm under pressure, and take care of people when they are vulnerable.Through the medical magnet program at my high school, I was able to get hands-on experience that most students don't get until much later. During ambulance ride-alongs with EMTs, I saw firsthand how fast pre-hospital emergencies move. The paramedics trusted me to place 12-lead EKGs and check vitals, which taught me how to keep a steady hand and focus on the patient even when a situation feels intense. In the hospital, getting to shadow different departments and stand in an operating room to observe a live surgery showed me how much discipline and teamwork go into patient care, especially when it comes to keeping sterile fields and communicating clearly.Outside the clinical setting, volunteering and working at blood drives for all four years of high school taught me how to provide comfort to patients. Whenever someone felt faint or dizzy after donating, it was up to me to monitor them, get them juice and snacks, and make sure they felt safe. That taught me attentiveness and how important it is to notice the small details in how someone is doing.Even competing in parliamentary procedure through HOSA and working customer service jobs at Just Salad and Little Caesars helped prepare me. HOSA taught me how to speak up under time pressure and work through formal decisions with a team, while food service taught me work ethic, multitasking, and keeping a positive attitude during busy rushes. All of these experiences have helped shape my discipline, time management, and passion for medicine as I continue on the pre-health track

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: My passion for veterinary medicine stems not only from my love for animals but also from my curiosity about the science. I knew I wanted to pursue a career in medicine and felt the need to advocate for animals, who speak a language we don't understand. Ultimately, that's what makes it more challenging, and I love a good challenge, especially anything related to problem-solving. Furthermore, I find it much more fascinating to learn about animal anatomy than human anatomy because there's so much to learn about animals across an incredible diversity of breeds and species. Throughout high school, I was part of the Vet program, where we groomed and cared for small animals during class. Even though these are great basic skills to learn, it made me realize I wanted to learn more about everything and take a deeper dive into vet medicine. One of the biggest eye-openers for me was doing a piglet dissection in the 9th grade. While everyone was disgusted by it, I actually enjoyed it, learning about and seeing the body parts and their functions, even the brain crumbling like scrambled eggs. It made me realize that there's more than just what meets the surface. Sometimes it's also not only about the animals but the owners as well, and helping them learn more about the animal that they care for and love, being that bridge of communication for them. My desire to learn more and always stay curious makes me more passionate about working with animals and being that advocate for them.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Joining this medical fraternity would provide the guidance, community, and support that are often difficult to find being on the pre-vet track. It’s also humorous that most of the time, when I say Pre-Vet, people often think I said Pre-Med. I am eager to surround myself with a driven, like-minded community; for me, I feel like I work better being surrounded by others who also have the same rigorous work as me. Professionally, I'm seeking guidance in wanting to know more about how to navigate my post-graduation path after four years at the University of Tampa. At the info session, it was briefly touched on internship and shadowing opportunities, which immediately caught my attention, as I struggle with finding these, as they mainly only take students who are already in vet school. I hope gaining insight into where current students have/currently interned, learning how to build professional connections, and receiving mentorship on the veterinary school application process would be valuable for my time here at the University. Furthermore, at the info session, the testimonies shared by current members, mainly talking about the sense of family and friends that they found being a part of MED, really encouraged me as someone who loves meeting new people and creating lifelong bonds. I love how MED also gives back to the community; being a Tampa native, that really means something to me as a girl who loves any chance to serve the very community that shaped my upbringing. Ultimately, I hope to gain a network of mentors and peers who will challenge me academically, while finding a campus family where I can truly belong and give back.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I bring a combination of academic resilience and strong communication skills that will allow me to contribute meaningfully to MED. My background as part of the vet program in high school has taught me to be highly adaptable and observant—skills I mastered during hands-on experiences like grooming and intricate animal dissections. Where others find it challenging to navigate veterinary medicine or deal with a difficult diagnostic puzzle, I see an exciting opportunity to problem-solve. I am eager to bring this mindset to MED, offering a fresh, diverse perspective to my peers. Furthermore, as someone who thrives on meeting new people and creating lifelong bonds, I am fully committed to strengthening our community. I am not looking to just be a passive member; I want to be an active, uplifting presence who encourages others through the rigorous workload. I am ready to step up, organize, and actively participate in our outreach initiatives, as I possess a deep, personal dedication to local community service. notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: My journey toward a healthcare career has been shaped by a blend of active student and public-facing roles. Together, these experiences have instilled in me the emotional resilience and clinical curiosity required of a healthcare professional. My understanding of veterinary medicine began in high school, where I enrolled in a four-year veterinary program. Responsibilities such as grooming and handling small animals taught me the vital healthcare skill of interpreting nonverbal patient behavior. Because animals cannot articulate their pain, I learned to remain calm and observant in difficult circumstances. While my peers were disgusted by the biological realities of a piglet dissection, I was intrigued by the intricate anatomy. I was taught to look beneath the surface to solve complex diagnostic puzzles. However, medical excellence goes beyond the lab; it relies heavily on collaboration and public engagement. On campus, participating in events with Happy Tails allowed me to champion animal welfare by bringing rescue animals to campus and fundraising for our local shelter, Mercy Full Project. Helping at events like these promoted public advocacy, showing others that you can find your forever friend through adoption. My customer-facing experience as a cashier at Publix further prepared me for high-stress environments. Managing peak rush hours and mastering swift conflict resolution taught me to remain calm and compassionate under pressure—a skill that can be directly linked to guiding anxious clients through veterinary medical emergencies. Finally, volunteering with Metropolitan Ministries solidified my commitment to empathetic care. Serving local families experiencing crisis taught me to connect authentically with people at all stages of life during vulnerable moments. My collective experiences—ranging from anatomical study to active on- and off-campus public service—have fully prepared me to manage the technical, emotional, and social responsibilities of a healthcare career.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I chose biology pre-med out of a passion for science. I found myself drawn not only to the science itself, but also to the way that scientific knowledge could be applied to directly improve a patient's health. That experience helped me realize that healthcare combines many of the things I value most: curiosity, problem-solving, continuous learning, and meaningful connections with others. I enjoy learning how different systems of the body interact and how small changes at the cellular or molecular level can have significant effects on a person’s overall health. At the same time, I want my education to have a purpose beyond understanding science in a classroom. I want to use that knowledge to help people make informed decisions about their health and feel supported throughout their care. My interest in healthcare has also grown from seeing how much trust patients place in their healthcare providers. Ultimately, I chose biology pre-med because it gives me the foundation to explore my passion for science while preparing me for a career where that knowledge can make a tangible difference in people’s lives. Healthcare is where I see my curiosity and desire to help others coming together.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare

In the emergency room, I saw how healthcare professionals must remain calm, attentive, and adaptable in unpredictable situations. My current position at the Wellness Center at Tampa has further developed my communication skills. It has also reinforced how important it is to listen to people and understand that everyone may need a different kind of support. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate complex ideas in an engaging and approachable way. Additionally, volunteering at Marklund in Geneva, Illinois, where I assisted individuals with severe disabilities during meals, activities, and sports, taught me the importance of patience, flexibility, and treating every individual with dignity. Together, these experiences have prepared me to enter healthcare with a more complete understanding of what it means to care for others. notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
For nearly six years, I planned to pursue a career in law since I'm strongly drawn to advocacy and the opportunity to make a difference within the legal system. When I was introduced to forensic science through the Criminal Justice System, however, I discovered a field that combined two of my greatest passions: science and advocacy. I immediately knew that forensic science was the path I wanted to pursue.

I am currently pursuing a B.S. in Forensic Science on the pre-pathology track, with minors in Biology and Spanish, and the goal of becoming a forensic pathologist. What excites me most about forensic pathology is the ability to combine medicine and science with the justice system. Forensic pathologists play an important role in understanding the circumstances surrounding a death and providing objective information that can assist families, investigators, attorneys, and the justice system.

My passion for healthcare comes from wanting to use my developing scientific knowledge and skills to serve others. I am especially interested in the medical side of forensic science and how medicine can provide answers when people and their families need them most. I see healthcare as another way to advocate for others, even when the advocacy takes place through science rather than a courtroom.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
What I hope to gain most from MED is guidance. As a student pursuing a B.S. in Forensic Science on the pre-pathology track, with the goal of becoming a forensic pathologist, I have found that my career path is not one that many students around me are pursuing. I have yet to meet another student on a forensic pathology track, and finding reliable information, mentorship, and guidance about the path to this career can be difficult. At times, it feels like I am walking in the dark trying to figure out what steps I should take next.

I hope MED can provide me with a community of students who understand the challenges of pursuing a career in healthcare and who are willing to share their experiences and knowledge. I want to learn from members who have already explored different areas of medicine, as well as from professionals and opportunities that MED can connect me with.

I also hope to gain a better understanding of what I should be doing now to prepare for my future. Whether that means learning about medical school, gaining relevant experience, developing professional connections, or simply having someone who can help me navigate the process, I believe MED could provide guidance that is difficult for me to find on my own.

Most importantly, I want to find a community where I can ask questions, learn from others, and know that I do not have to navigate my path alone.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
I would bring a combination of curiosity, determination, attention to detail, adaptability, and a strong desire to serve others to MED. I am someone who genuinely enjoys learning and asking questions, especially when I encounter something I do not understand. My education in forensic science has taught me to approach problems analytically, consider multiple perspectives, and recognize the importance of accuracy and evidence when reaching a conclusion.

I also believe one of my greatest strengths is my determination. I have chosen a highly specialized career path and have continued pursuing it even when finding information and guidance has been difficult. Rather than allowing uncertainty to discourage me, I have learned to seek out answers and create opportunities to learn for myself.

I would also bring a unique perspective to MED. To my knowledge, I would be the first member pursuing a concentration in pathology, specifically forensic pathology. This would allow me to contribute knowledge and perspectives from the intersection of medicine, forensic science, and the criminal justice system. I hope to use that perspective not only to learn from other members, but also to give back by sharing what I learn with the organization.

I want to make an impact on MED by being an engaged member who contributes to discussions, supports other students, and brings a perspective that may not otherwise be represented. I believe the best organizations are ones where members both gain from the experience and give something meaningful back, and that is the kind of member I hope to be.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My experiences in Mock Trial, at the Dream Center, and through my internship with the Metropolitan Nashville Crime Lab have each helped prepare me for the responsibilities of a future career in healthcare.

Mock Trial has taught me how important communication, preparation, teamwork, and attention to detail are. As someone who originally planned to pursue law, Mock Trial gave me an opportunity to develop my advocacy skills and learn how to communicate information effectively. These skills will remain valuable in healthcare, where professionals must communicate with patients, families, colleagues, and other professionals.

My work at the Dream Center has strengthened my understanding of service and responsibility. Working with children has taught me to be dependable, patient, and willing to contribute wherever I am needed. Healthcare is ultimately a service-oriented field, and I believe understanding the importance of treating people with respect and compassion is just as important as having strong technical knowledge.

My summer internship with the Metropolitan Nashville Crime Lab provided another important perspective. Being exposed to multiple sciences reinforced my interest in forensic science while teaching me about professionalism, accountability, and the importance of accuracy. It also helped me understand how different professionals must work together to serve the public effectively. As someone pursuing forensic pathology, I know that my future career will require me to collaborate with people across medicine and the criminal justice system.

Together, these experiences have helped me develop the communication, teamwork, professionalism, attention to detail, and sense of service that I will need in healthcare. They have also confirmed that I want a career where I can use science and my ability to advocate for others to make a meaningful difference.

I hope to bring that same initiative to MED while learning from the other members and contributing to a positive and supportive community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
My extracurricular experiences have prepared me for a career in healthcare by teaching me how to work with others, take responsibility, and serve my community. One of my most meaningful experiences has been founding Baking for the Better, a nonprofit focused on supporting people experiencing homelessness. Through the organization, I have organized fundraisers, events, and outreach, and provided meals, clothing, and other essential goods to people in need. This experience taught me to recognize the needs of others and take initiative to help, and it gave me a passion for service, which I believe will be important when caring for patients.

My leadership experiences have further developed my ability to communicate and work with others. Through positions such as being a State officer for Key Club, a leader of a club that worked with special needs students, and a Club President, I have learned how to organize events, collaborate with different groups, and take responsibility for a team. These experiences have prepared me to communicate effectively with patients and work alongside other healthcare professionals.

Additionally, shadowing for over 100 hours in general dentistry, orthodontics, pediatrics, and periodontics has given me firsthand exposure to healthcare. I have seen how dentists use their technical knowledge while also taking the time to communicate with and reassure patients. This showed me that healthcare is not simply about treating a problem, but about making patients feel comfortable and cared for.

Overall, my experiences have given me a better understanding of what it means to work in healthcare and have prepared me to approach my future career with a strong sense of service and responsibility.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text:
My interest in pursuing a career as a physician assistant began through my own experiences with surgery and rehabilitation. During my recovery, I had an amazing orthopedic surgeon and physician assistant whom I still look up to today. Their funny, positive, and bubbly personalities made me feel comfortable and safe during such a hard time in my life. I especially admired my physician assistant because her responsibilities were just as important to my care as my surgeon’s, while she worked alongside and supported the surgeon rather than being the primary leader. I realized this type of role fits my personality because I would rather work as part of a team and support a physician than be the person in charge. I also love that physician assistants can work in different areas of healthcare and have the flexibility to change specialties throughout their careers. I find this exciting because I want a career where I can continue learning and exploring different fields.

I have always been an empathetic and caring person, so I knew I wanted a career focused on helping others. My experiences as a patient showed me how much compassion and genuine care from a healthcare provider can impact someone's recovery. I hope to provide that same comfort and support to my future patients, especially children. I chose Allied Health because it allows me to explore both the physician assistant and physical therapy paths, which are two healthcare fields that interest me.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text:
As a transfer student, I came into this year with a better understanding of what college is like and a clearer idea of what I want to accomplish. My main goals this year are to become more involved on campus, improve my GPA, especially in my science courses, and take more steps toward my future career as a physician assistant through clubs, internships, and other opportunities.When I attended the involvement fair, I was immediately drawn to MED because I felt that it fit my values of a community I’d want to be a part of. I hope to gain a deeper understanding of the physician assistant career and learn more about the steps I should be taking to get into PA school in the future. I also hope MED will provide me with resources, guidance, and support that can help me become a stronger student and improve academically.
Beyond academics and my career, I want to become more involved in a community where I can meet people who share similar interests and values. I hope to build genuine life long relationships and friendships. Most importantly, I hope to be a part of a welcoming and nonjudgmental environment where I feel comfortable being myself, learning from others, and growing alongside people who have similar goals.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text:
Some skills I would contribute to MED are my ability to work well with groups and my approachable, friendly personality. I love talking, meeting new people, and I can adapt very easily to new environments and different personalities. I also really enjoy volunteering and want to become more involved in it this year, so I would be consistent with attending and participating in MED events. 

I also believe I have strong leadership qualities. If I were accepted into MED, I would want to work toward becoming a good candidate for future leadership or social media roles. Although I am still working on improving my time management and organization, I am very persistent and driven, especially when it comes to improving my academics this year. Even though my grades may not currently exceed MED’s requirements, I am committed to improving them and putting in the effort to reach my academic goals.

I want to meet people who share similar interests and goals, and I believe being able to connect with others and make them feel comfortable is something I would contribute to MED. I value people who are genuine and supportive, and I hope to bring those same qualities to the organization. I think all these qualities would allow me to make a positive contribution to the MED community.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text:
I think my job as a lifeguard for the past three summers has been one of the biggest experiences that has prepared me for a career in healthcare. I had to become CPR and First Aid certified, and although I was fortunate that I did not have to make saves often, the one time I did gave me a real understanding of the emergency aspect of healthcare. Realizing that someone’s life is in your hands is a crazy thing to experience, and you do not truly understand the pressure until you are actually in an emergency situation. I am really grateful that lifeguarding gave me that experience.

My volunteer experiences, whether it was coaching children with special needs or spending time socializing with the elderly to keep them company, have also made me much more empathetic. I believe empathy is one of the most important qualities in healthcare. You cannot go into healthcare only for the money or benefits, you have to genuinely care about your patients, and I think that's something that will come naturally to me.

Lastly, my participation in sports throughout my life has played a major role in preparing me for healthcare because it is what sparked my interest in the field in the first place. Through my many sports-related injuries, I have visited athletic trainers, hospitals, orthopedic offices, and physical therapy offices countless times. My own physician assistant also took the time to explain the degrees and programs she went through and what her lifestyle was like as a PA. Hearing about her journey helped me better understand the responsibility that comes with this career and how important academics are to reaching my goals. It made me realize that I need to take my academics more seriously and step up my effort to prepare myself for the future. These experiences have given me a general understanding of different healthcare positions and helped me learn what I would and would not want in a future career.

notes.brother: From their application: Why this major / passion for healthcare
notes.text: I wanted to be a Lawyer for the longest time, but throughout Highschool I found myself being more interested in my STEM classes over my ELA classes especially my senior year of high school when I took Organic Chemistry. A hard class don’t get me wrong, but it was so rewarding when I understood a topic and learned about the compounds and structures that make up Chemistry. I then chose Biochemistry because I knew I wanted chemistry in my Major and that if I wanted to go to Med school most of my classes I needed to basically make up the Biochemistry Major. After my Lawyer dreams died my mom had always noticed that I never was squeamish around blood and/or bodily fluids she suggested I look into a medical career. To humor her I went to a medical convention where we watched a live shoulder rotator cuff surgery which to me was the coolest thing ever. I found it fascinating that medical professionals had found ways to fix one another in such a non-invasive way because in this surgery they had only cut three incisions in the woman's arm to fix her rotator cuff. From there I knew I wanted to do something that involved the OR because I found surgeries fascinating.

notes.brother: From their application: What they hope to gain from MED
notes.text: Based on what I have heard through one of my cousins who is in med school and anyone who has gone through med school is that half the struggle is getting into med school. Through MED I hope to improve my chances of getting into med school. By gaining a mentor and friends that are going through the same thing, and to motivate one another because I am personally better at studying, and doing school work when I collaborate with others. Having a mentor like a  big or just an older student would also be a big help to give me advice along the way on what things I should be doing each year of college and the things that are less important. I also plan to take advantage of any volunteer, research, and shadowing opportunities that MED offers because I want to experience all the opportunities that Tampa has to offer, and get a feel for the field that I want to get into.

notes.brother: From their application: Skills and traits they'd bring
notes.text: I am a very driven person so in the future if there is ever something that needs to be done last minute or if something is just not working I would make it my sole responsibility to make it work. Whether that is to go to find sponsors and email a bunch of companies or to cold email/spam companies to request for volunteer work, shadowing hours, or to get a guest speaker I would be determined to make it happen. I am extraverted so I don't mind going up to random people and talking to them like someone who is in MED who seems to not be talking to others and feeling left out or giving presentations to other about MED.

notes.brother: From their application: Experience preparing them for healthcare
notes.text: Ever since I was fifteen I have been First Aid, CPR, and AED certified, so I have always had a critical foundation for healthcare careers and am aware of the seriousness that comes with the certifications in performing them. I used these certifications while I was a life guard as well as being a camp counselor. This past summer I was a camp counselor. It has taught me many skills that I would never have thought would be so important like getting to know who you are caring for in order to help them because everyone needs different attention to feel cared for . For example when the little kids were homesick reading to one of the girls would help her go to bed, but another girl needed me to talk to her about random things to get her mind off missing her mom, and another girl needed me to sit on the edge of her bed so she wouldn’t feel alone. It isn’t just about caring for people but it is finding out the right care for them. Camp counseling also taught me that no matter how much training you are given you are going to be given scenarios where you have to make decisions on the fly based on your best judgement. Also last year I also went to a medical program at UC Berkeley where we had a lot of hands-on experience like suturing a pig's foot and drawing blood on a dummy. Which gave me a perspective on how much precision is needed when being a medical professional.
